Whatever the line of sight meets - a block or an entity - is the impact point. Blocks stop the trace, so a wall between the user and open ground is where the technique lands.

A miss lands in mid-air

With nothing in the way, the point is range blocks along the look vector, not the ground under it: aiming at the sky puts the impact in the sky. An ability that should fall back to the terrain reads the heightmap at that point itself — that is a different answer from the one this method gives, and GlitteringStorm in AwakenAwakenNoMi deliberately wants the other one.

It is measured from the eyes, so a crouching user does not aim from their feet.

docs.title: sizedRange
docs.text:
A range given for a player's body, grown to fit whatever the caster is morphed into:

float reach = AkumaTargeting.sizedRange(entity, REACH);
LivingEntity target = AkumaTargeting.firstInSight(entity, reach);

A morph pushes every target away from the caster's eyes

Ranges are traced from the eye position. A big form puts those high above the ground and far behind the chest: the awakened Brachiosaurus Guard Point is 5.5 x 10.5 blocks with its eyes at 10, so a target standing 8 blocks in front of its feet is already 12.8 blocks from its eyes. A flat reach tuned on a player is unusable there - which is how NeckCatapultAbility shipped (AwakenAwakenNoMi#402).

The extra is the caster's own bulk, its eye height plus half its width, so the number in your ability keeps meaning "this far in front of me" in every form. A player gains about 1.9 blocks; that Guard Point gains about 12.7.

Use it for anything reaching out of the caster - a pick-up range, a line, a cone, a grab. Not for an area centred on the caster: that radius is already measured from the body rather than from the eyes.

docs.title: inCone
docs.text:
Whether a target stands inside a cone around where the user is looking:

for (LivingEntity target : this.rangeComponent.getTargetsInArea(entity, 6.0F)) {
    if (target != entity && AkumaTargeting.inCone(entity, target, 45.0F)) {
        // inside a 90 degree fan in front of the user
    }
}

The angle is half the opening: 45 is a 90 degree fan. A target standing exactly on the user counts as inside, so a cone never refuses point-blank contact.

When a press finds nothing. A technique that finds no target should still cost something, or a held key becomes a free scanner: AkumaAbilityHelper.FAILED_PRESS_COOLDOWN (10 ticks), not zero and not the full cooldown. A refusal, such as a protected area or a creative target, costs the same. And give the player a cue that nothing was hit, such as a whiff sound.

docs.title: Deferred work: AkumaTickQueue
docs.text:
Work to run on a later server tick — at the end of this one, or a fixed number of ticks from now.

AkumaTickQueue.run(() -> strike(holder, target));            // end of this tick
AkumaTickQueue.runIn(30, () -> aftershock(holder, target));  // 30 ticks from now

docs.title: What it is for
docs.text:
A hurt event that has to land a second blow. Dealing it from inside the triggering LivingHurtEvent does not work: vanilla has already set lastHurt to that blow's amount and silently drops anything weaker, and the listeners reading the event see the second blow as a fresh one. So the blow is queued and delivered once the tick is over.

Four fruits in AwakenAwakenNoMi had written that by hand before #443 — two as an end-of-tick List<Runnable>, two as a per-entry countdown — and no two agreed on the details.

docs.title: The four decisions it carries
docs.text:
Why it matters the list is snapshotted before the drain a task that queues another is reachable — a queued blow fires a hurt event the fruit's own listener reads — and would otherwise be a ConcurrentModificationException anything queued during a drain waits for the next tick a task cannot make itself run again in the same drain a task that throws does not take the rest with it it is logged and the drain carries on the queue is dropped when the server stops a static queue of closures over LivingEntitys otherwise holds them across a world reload

That last one is not hypothetical: of the four hand-written copies, one had no shutdown clear at all.

There is deliberately no shared am I draining flag

The obvious extra is a global re-entry guard, so one fruit's listener ignores another fruit's deferred blow. It would also mean any queued work muting every fruit's on-hit reaction for the length of the drain — a behaviour change nothing established as wanted, and a blow landing thirty ticks later is a real blow that other systems ought to see. A fruit that needs to ignore its own strike keeps its own flag, raised around its own task.

Server side only

ServerTickEvent does not fire on a client with no integrated server, so a task queued from client code would never run. Queue from the server thread.

docs.title: The delay is in ticks the server ran
docs.text: Not in game time, so it does not drift with /tick freeze or a paused single-player world.

docs.title: ServerScopedMap
docs.text:
Since 3.1.0. A static map that belongs to the running server, not to the game. In single player the same game opens world after world, and a plain static map carries one world's entries into the next: a last-use game time from a world at tick 1,000,000 blocked an ability for hours in a new one.

private static final ServerScopedMap<UUID, Long> LAST_USE = ServerScopedMap.perPlayer();
private static final ServerScopedMap<GlobalPos, BlockState> MARKED = ServerScopedMap.create();

create() is emptied when the server stops; perPlayer(), keyed by player UUID, also drops a player's entry when they log out. It is a HashMap otherwise: game thread only.

docs.title: AbilityLifecycle
docs.text:
Since 3.1.0. What the base mod leaves undone when an ability is cut short.

Death. The base mod ticks abilities only while their holder is alive and ends none of them when it dies: a continuous ability never reaches its end event, so whatever it put in the world or on the body stays. Opt in from your mod constructor, and every running ability of your namespace is stopped, end event included, as its holder dies:

AbilityLifecycle.stopOnDeath(MODID);

Losing the fruit needs nothing: Ability.onRemove already stops the continuity.

Zero gravity. NoGravity is saved with the entity: a server stopped during a float left the player floating at the next login. Use noGravity(entity) / endNoGravity(entity) instead of setNoGravity, and a login lifts a marked one.

Soft landings. A "the next fall is free" flag lived until a fall used it, and landing in water used none: it cancelled some later, unrelated fall. grantSoftLanding(entity, key) opens a 20-second window; useSoftLanding(entity, key) in your LivingFallEvent spends it.

docs.title: Titles
docs.text:
A title is a name a player earns and may wear: shown after their name in the player list, gold on grey, Name - Chef of the Baratie. Players pick theirs in the Titles screen, the "Titles" plank of Mine Mine no Mi's character screen: titles by category, the held ones in ink, the worn one in gold, the rest greyed with how to earn them.

Titles come from three places, all alike once loaded:

  • a mod's code, AkumaTitles.register;
  • a profession's level titles, Profession.withTitle;
  • a data pack, data/<namespace>/titles/<path>.json.

A player holds a title while its condition is met, or once a mod has granted it to them. They wear one at a time; a worn title they stop holding (a level lost, another trade chosen in Crew mode) is hidden, and comes back with it.

docs.title: Profession titles
docs.text:
() -> new Profession(ProfessionKind.CRAFTING)
        .withTitle(25, "mymod.title.cook.25")
        .withTitle(100, "mymod.title.cook.100")

Each is held from its level on, in a profession the player practises, and listed in the Professions category, a trade's titles together. Its id is <namespace>:profession/<path>/<level>: AkumaTitles.professionTitleId(profession, level). A profession has at most one title per level: getTitles() lists them as LevelTitle(level, translationKey), and getTitle(level) gives the one granted at exactly that level, or null.

docs.title: A mod's titles
docs.text:
AkumaTitles.register(Title.builder(new ResourceLocation(MODID, "sky_king"),
                Component.translatable("mymod.title.sky_king"))
        .category(new ResourceLocation(MODID, "exploration"))
        .icon(() -> new ItemStack(MyItems.CLOUD.get()))
        .description(Component.translatable("mymod.title.sky_king.how"))
        .build());

Register once, before the server starts (common setup). Then, on the server:

Call Does AkumaTitles.grant(player, id) Gives the title for good, whatever its condition. The id need not be loaded yet. AkumaTitles.revoke(player, id) Takes a granted title back. AkumaTitles.wear(player, id) Wears it, or none with null; refused if the player does not hold it. AkumaTitles.getWorn(player) The title worn, if still held. AkumaTitles.held(player) Every title held. AkumaTitles.refresh(player) Checks the conditions again and tells the client and the player list.

The builder's other options: iconTexture (a square texture of any size, drawn in place of the item), order (lowest first, then by name), hidden (listed only once held), and condition:

Condition Held when TitleCondition.GRANTED (default) granted only TitleCondition.professionLevel(profession, level) at that level, practising the profession TitleCondition.advancement(id) the advancement is done your own TitleCondition test(ServerPlayer) is true

A Title gives all of it back: getName(), getCategory(), getOrder(), isHidden() and getCondition().

Conditions are checked again on every profession progress sync, advancement, login and reload. A condition of your own that changes at another time needs an AkumaTitles.refresh(player).

A category's name is the translation of title_category.<namespace>.<path>, or its path, capitalised. akumalib:professions is listed first, akumalib:general (a title's default) last.

docs.title: Data pack titles
docs.text:
data/mypack/titles/storm_chaser.json:

{
  "name": { "text": "Storm Chaser" },
  "description": { "text": "Sail through a storm" },
  "category": "mypack:events",
  "icon": "minecraft:trident",
  "order": 10,
  "hidden": false,
  "condition": { "type": "advancement", "advancement": "mypack:storm/chaser" }
}

Only name is needed (a text component, translate works too). The conditions are {"type": "advancement", "advancement": id}, {"type": "profession", "profession": id, "level": n}, and {"type": "granted"}, which is also what no condition means. A data pack title cannot replace a mod's; a file that does not parse is logged and skipped. /reload picks up changes.

docs.title: Tooltips
docs.text: Ready-made advanced description lines for the ability screen, built on the base mod's AbilityStat.

docs.title: Explosion stats: ToolTipHelper
docs.text:
.addAdvancedDescriptionLine(ToolTipHelper.getExplosionTooltips(power, size, damage))

Adds an "Explosion" heading followed by power, size and damage lines. Each line is skipped when its value is 0 or less.

The damage shown is the number you pass

An AbilityExplosion with setStaticDamage deals its value without the x0.4 factor, so pass the real value here, not a scaled one. See Damage.

docs.title: Zone stats: AwakenTooltipHelper
docs.text:
.addAdvancedDescriptionLine(AbilityDescriptionLine.NEW_LINE,
        AwakenTooltipHelper.getZoneRadiusTooltip(MAX_ZONE_SIZE),
        AwakenTooltipHelper.getEffectTickTooltip(EFFECTS_TICK_INTERVAL))
Method Shows getZoneRadiusTooltip(maxRadius) the largest radius the zone reaches, in blocks getEffectTickTooltip(ticks) how often the zone applies its effect, in seconds

Both lines are skipped for a value of 0 or less.

docs.title: Library translation keys: AkumaI18n
docs.text:
The translation keys the library's own base classes and tooltip helpers use:

Constant Used by ABILITY_DESCRIPTION_STAT_NAME_EXPLOSION, _SIZE, _POWER ToolTipHelper ABILITY_DESCRIPTION_STAT_NAME_ZONE_RADIUS, _EFFECT_PULSE AwakenTooltipHelper MESSAGE_GROUND_ONLY ensureOnGroundOrNotify, when a ground-only technique is used in mid-air MESSAGE_MISSING_MATERIALS CraftingAbility's default message, when the materials are missing

The library ships their English text. Keys for your own fruits and abilities belong in your addon's lang file.

A key missing from the lang file shows raw

Registering a name supplies a default, but the client renders from the lang file: a key with no entry appears as the raw key in the tooltip, and nothing fails at build time.

docs.title: Damage source metadata the icons cannot show: AkumaSourceTooltip
docs.text:
Since 2.9.0. The base mod shows an ability's haki nature, source types and element (setSourceHakiNature, setSourceType, setSourceElement on the builder) as a row of small icons after its name, and nothing else. A value with no texture is not drawn: the elements SLIME, RUBBER, RUST, GRAVITY and the type INDIRECT (and AIR before 2.11.0, which now has its icon: see Fixes to the base mod). They still change the fight, so say it in words:

.addAdvancedDescriptionLine(AbilityDescriptionLine.NEW_LINE,
        CooldownComponent.getTooltip(COOLDOWN),
        DealDamageComponent.getTooltip(DAMAGE),
        AkumaSourceTooltip.iconless(),                  // "Source Indirect", read from the core
        AkumaSourceTooltip.pierces(true, true))         // "Pierces Armour, Logia"
Method Shows iconless() the core's icon-less element and types, read when the tooltip is drawn; skipped when every value has an icon pierces(armour, logia) flags applied at hit time (addGlobalPiercing, bypassLogia), which the metadata cannot carry describe(core) the iconless() text for a core, or null

SourceType.LOGIA_BYPASS is read nowhere in the base mod and has no icon: declare the hit-time bypassLogia() and show it with pierces(false, true).

docs.title: World events
docs.text:
Since 2.8.0. A mod can bring events to the world, the way Mine Mine no Mi brings its caravans and Celestial Dragon visits: they come on their own now and then near a player, are announced in the chat, are sold as rumours by the base mod's barkeepers, and end on time. Cruise Cruise no Mi's merchant ship, Sea King and wreck are world events.

Mine Mine no Mi's own list of events is fixed in its code, closed to addons. AkumaLib runs a scheduler of its own, on the same model.

docs.title: A type of event
docs.text:
Extend WorldEventType and register one instance:

public final class StormEvent extends WorldEventType {

    public static final StormEvent INSTANCE = new StormEvent();

    private StormEvent() {
        super(new ResourceLocation(MODID, "storm"));
    }

    @Override
    public boolean isEnabled() { return MyConfig.STORMS.get(); }          // new ones may start

    @Override
    public long nextStartDelay(RandomSource random) { return 5 * DAY; }  // from one start to the next

    @Override
    public Optional<BlockPos> findPlace(ServerLevel level, ServerPlayer player, RandomSource random, CompoundTag data) {
        return Optional.of(player.blockPosition().offset(200, 0, 0));    // or empty: not this time
    }

    @Override
    public long duration(RandomSource random) { return DAY; }

    @Override
    public boolean start(ServerLevel level, WorldEvent event) { ... return true; }   // false: nothing starts

    @Override
    public void tick(ServerLevel level, WorldEvent event) { ... }         // once a second while it runs

    @Override
    public void end(ServerLevel level, WorldEvent event) { ... }          // undo what start did

    @Override
    public Component startMessage(WorldEvent event) { ... }              // to every player; null for none
}

AkumaWorldEvents.register(StormEvent.INSTANCE);   // once, before the server starts
Method Default What it is isEnabled() true whether new ones may start; running ones still end on time nextStartDelay(random) - ticks from one start to the next, drawn each time; also the wait before the first one retryDelay() 1200 ticks before trying again when no place was found or start refused maxRunning() 1 how many may run at once findPlace(...) - where, near the chosen player; data is the new event's own tag, to fill with what start needs duration(random) - how long one lasts, in ticks start / tick / end - / nothing / - what happens startMessage / warningMessage / endMessage null told to every player; the warning warningTicks() before the end (an in-game hour) rumour(event) null what a barkeeper says of it rumourRange() 2000 how far from the barkeeper it may be and still be his rumour

Times are game time ticks: they run on while players sleep, and do not jump with /time set.

docs.title: What runs
docs.text:
A WorldEvent is one occurrence: its id(), type(), pos(), startTime(), endTime(), and its own data() tag, where start writes whatever end will need (what it placed, where). Events are saved with the Overworld: they survive a restart and end on time.

The scheduler runs once a second, in the Overworld only. When a type's next start is due and fewer than maxRunning() run, it picks a random player there, asks findPlace, and starts the event. A type's code that throws is logged, never passed on to the tick.

AkumaWorldEvents also gives: running(server), running(server, type), get(server, id), startNear(player, type) and startAt(level, type, pos, data) (for commands and tests; the schedule is left as it is), stop(server, id), nextStart and setNextStart.

Placing something big

findPlace and start run on the server thread: whatever they cost, the server waits. Do not generate chunks to look at them, and put a large structure down in tick, once level.hasChunksAt(...) says its chunks are loaded, as Mine Mine no Mi does for its caravans.

docs.title: Rumours
docs.text:
When a player pays a Mine Mine no Mi barkeeper for a rumour (1,000 Belly, the base mod's price), a running event within its type's rumourRange() of the barkeeper can be the answer: the nearest one with a rumour. Otherwise the base mod answers as before.

In Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5, a barkeeper answers "nothing new" to any player who is not a Marine or a Bounty Hunter, whatever it knows. Such a player now hears of the world events near the barkeeper. A Marine hears the base mod's own rumour half the time.

docs.title: For operators
docs.text: Command Does /akumalib events list what runs, and when each type is next tried /akumalib events start <type> starts one near you, now /akumalib events stop <id> ends one now, as if its time were up /akumalib events next <type> <seconds> when the scheduler next tries that type

docs.title: Worldgen and dimensions
docs.text: What an addon needs to shape terrain of its own, or a whole dimension: the registers for its codecs and types, and four tools for the questions worldgen code keeps running into.

docs.title: The registers
docs.text:
Your AkumaRegistry carries a deferred register for each of these, like every other kind of entry. Put every one you fill on the mod event bus, as in Getting started.

Register For FLUIDS, FLUID_TYPES fluids, and the type that says how one behaves (swimming, boats, fog) DENSITY_FUNCTION_TYPES, BIOME_SOURCES, CHUNK_GENERATORS, FEATURES, PLACEMENT_MODIFIER_TYPES terrain of your own: their codecs and types, the instances coming from datagen STRUCTURE_TYPES, STRUCTURE_PLACEMENT_TYPES, STRUCTURE_PIECE_TYPES structures; a piece type left unregistered loses its structure on reload

docs.title: The tools
docs.text:
• Cell grids

    AkumaCells: a deterministic grid of jittered cells, so several readers agree on where a feature is.

  • Asking the overworld

    OverworldLookup: the overworld's biome and seed from another dimension's worldgen thread, without loading a chunk.

  • Dimension travel

    AkumaDimensionTravel: send a body, its vehicle and its riders to another dimension with a velocity that survives.

  • Jigsaw pools

    AkumaJigsaw: add pieces (features, templates) to another mod's jigsaw pools.

docs.title: Awaken Awaken no Mi
docs.text:
Awaken Awaken no Mi adds awakenings to the Devil Fruits of Mine Mine no Mi: new abilities, and for Zoan fruits new awakened forms, that a fruit's user gets once their fruit is awakened.

Version documented 2.1.0 Mod id awakenawakennomi Download CurseForge Changelog Every release

docs.title: What it adds
docs.text:
• 225 awakened abilities across 70 of the base mod's Devil Fruits (see Fruits).
  • Awakened Zoan forms: the awakened version of each supported Zoan's point forms, with their own models and animations.
  • Domains: area abilities that change the ground around the user, such as Kenzan World, Smooth World or Sabaku no Okoku.
  • BakuMetal gear: a BakuMetal Ingot and a full set of BakuMetal tools and armour, each with a crafting recipe.
  • Custom status effects, particles and sounds for the new abilities.

It adds no new Devil Fruit: every ability here belongs to a fruit the base mod already has.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Mod Version Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge 47.4.18 or later Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.x (built against 1.20.1-0.11.5) AkumaLib 2.6.1 or later

AkumaLib is required

AkumaLib is a library: it adds nothing you can see, but this mod is built on it. Without it, Forge stops on its missing-dependency screen. Since 2.1.0, Awaken Awaken no Mi needs AkumaLib 2.6.1 or newer.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
1. Install Forge for Minecraft 1.20.1, then put Mine Mine no Mi, AkumaLib and Awaken Awaken no Mi in your mods folder.
  2. Eat one of the supported fruits. Its awakened abilities are added to the fruit's kit, but stay locked.
  3. Awaken the fruit. The awakened abilities unlock once the base mod considers your fruit awakened.

This mod does not decide when a fruit awakens

Awaken Awaken no Mi contains the awakened forms and abilities only. The progression that awakens a fruit lives elsewhere:

  • In survival, install Awaken Path. It awakens a player's fruit once they reach a Doriki threshold and have kept the fruit long enough.
  • Without Awaken Path, a fruit can only be awakened by a command, or by another addon.

docs.title: Awakening with a command
docs.text:
The base mod's ability command has an awaken option:

/ability awaken [targets]

Without targets, it applies to the player running it. It needs the command's permission, and the base mod's Enable Awakenings option must be on. That option is off by default; Awaken Path switches it on for you.

It is a toggle

Run on a fruit that is already awakened, the command removes the awakening.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Every Awaken Awaken no Mi release for Minecraft 1.20.1, newest first, as published on CurseForge. The Minecraft 1.16.5 releases (0.2.1 to 0.7.2) are listed there too.

Released 2026-09-28 · Download

⚠️ AkumaLib update required: 2.6.1

This version needs AkumaLib 2.6.1 or newer. With an older AkumaLib the game will stop on Forge's missing-dependency screen.

Just replace the AkumaLib jar in your mods folder with the new one.

A bug-fix release. Every awakening was put through a full audit, then tested in game ability by ability: more than sixty fixes, from crashes to tooltips. A few mechanics the abilities always promised now work for the first time - Ice Epoch and Meigo no Jidai's lasting zone, jumping on your Cake Golem, Nikyu no Itami absorbing blows.

Now working as described
  • Ice Epoch and Meigo no Jidai: after a full charge, the land stays frozen (or molten) for 60 seconds. Enemies who stay inside are frozen or set ablaze again every 2 seconds; you and your allies are spared
  • Cake Golem: you can jump while riding your golem - hold space longer for a higher jump
  • Nikyu no Itami: absorbs a fifth of each blow while its gauge has room, as its description always said
  • Mogu Heavy Point: the form now gives Haste and Night Vision
  • Scrap Field and String Weave slow players too, not only mobs. Heavy iron armour makes the Scrap Field much slower
  • Hide and Seek: one hunt at a time. A second Doa user is told the pocket dimension is busy instead of throwing both groups into the same arena
Fixes Crashes and freezes
  • The game no longer crashes when Rust, Inferno, Friction, Magma Burn, Molten Armor, Sugar Coffin, Meigo no Jidai or Glittering Tornado hurt someone after going through a portal
  • Airburst sets off about seven explosions again, not a hundred and fifty: the freeze is gone
  • Spin (Kame) no longer hits twice as often as it should
Damage and numbers
  • Ursus Calamiti deals its real damage
  • Deadweight pulses go from 16 to 48, 160 in all, as the tooltip says
  • Asshuku reaches its full 135 damage without needing Shinokuni
  • Neck Catapult's tooltip shows the real 60 damage
  • Inga Samsara and Shared Fate echo the blows you actually take, once per hit - no longer every tick you stand in lava or fire
  • Resonating World and Shadow Marionette stop working once their user logs out or dies
Allies and enemies
  • Candle World, Sabaku no Okoku, Ever White, Assign World, Yukiro and Soul Reap no longer hurt your crewmates, pets or allies
  • Taiki, Sabaku no Okoku and Mogu Heavy Point no longer take away potions you drank (Regeneration, Speed, Haste...) when their effect ends
Movement and falls
  • Neck Catapult, Ivory Catastrophe and the other throws no longer launch the target 40 blocks up when you look straight down
  • Weight Shift really cancels fall damage, and Zenith protects from any height
  • Downdraft no longer adds a second fall on top of its slam
  • Dai Hanpatsu on yourself: you land and stop rising
  • A mob released by Undertow no longer falls through the world
  • Ukiyo lifts its targets to 22 blocks and holds them there, instead of letting them climb out of sight; an arrow that drifts out of the zone falls again
  • Ending Waterpool Domain while swimming underground no longer leaves you stuck in the rock
  • Crown of Flames no longer lets you fly while its passive is blocked (Seastone, a protected area)
Charges and cooldowns
  • Charges finish properly under a faster ability time (Reverse Slow): Bubble Cage, Soul Reap, K-Room and a dozen others no longer fizzle after a full charge
  • Pressing One Man Army, Fiddle Overdrive, Reverse Slow or Diffraction again ends them instead of starting over
  • Interrupting Ice Epoch or Meigo no Jidai (water, Seastone) costs a share of the cooldown, not two seconds
The world around you
  • Piercing Blast, Titan Smash, Titan Trample, Tenchi Hokai and Ice Epoch respect ability griefing and protected areas, block by block. Ice Epoch no longer turns chests into ice
  • Break White's web always goes away, even if its user logs out or leaves the dimension
  • Yukiro's wall gives back everything it replaced - grass, flowers, vines, snow
  • Scrap Tempest no longer tears down your field when you cannot pay for the cast
Summons
  • Cake Golem and the Diosa Fleur clone keep their size, health and will to fight after you walk away and come back
  • The Cake Golem's attack swing shows, and it only drops its cakes when an enemy beats it
  • Living Gate: projectiles swallowed before a relog come back out; a skeleton's arrow sent back can no longer be picked up
  • Hide and Seek: if the hunter logs out, the captured mobs go back to where they were taken, not to the world spawn
Visuals, sounds and text
  • Barrier Eruption: the ring of panels forms a clean circle and can be seen from any distance
  • Total Isolation and Spirit Seal show their coloured veil in third person
  • Titan: crouching under a ceiling no longer lets the camera see through it
  • Netsuryo's heat display reaches 0 and 100 instead of stopping just short
  • On the Beat: a combo carried over a relog or a respawn now lapses
  • Burning effects no longer hiss as if put out every time a blow stacks them
  • Ability Seal no longer frees abilities another effect keeps disabled
  • The High Frequency Wall block has a name, and Cake Golem and Crown Flight have proper names
  • Storm Sovereign's description gives the real protection against conductive attacks
Requirements
  • Minecraft 1.20.1
  • Forge 47.4.18+
  • Mine Mine no Mi 1.20.1-0.11.5
  • AkumaLib 2.6.1+

Released 2026-09-18 · Download

⚠️ AkumaLib update required: 2.4.0

This version needs AkumaLib 2.4.0 or newer. With an older AkumaLib the game will stop on Forge's missing-dependency screen.

Just replace the AkumaLib jar in your mods folder with the new one.

Every awakening is now complete. Every Paramecia and Logia awakening has at least three abilities, and every Zoan has all of its awakened forms plus two abilities beside them. This release adds 77 new awakened abilities, bringing the mod to 70 fruits and 225 awakened abilities.

Every awakening was also gone over while its fruit was extended: numbers brought up to a fight against an armoured 250 HP player, promised mechanics that did nothing made real, missing sounds, poses and tooltips added, and icons redrawn where they did not read.

New Content New Awakened Abilities

Paramecia

  • Awa Awa no Mi: Bubble Cage, Squeaky Clean
  • Baku Baku no Mi: Armor Munch, Iron Stomach
  • Bane Bane no Mi: Ricochet
  • Bara Bara no Mi: Bara Bara Parade, Severed Grip
  • Beta Beta no Mi: Beta Beta Surge, Slick Passage
  • Chiyu Chiyu no Mi: Cellular Overgrowth, Overflow
  • Doa Doa no Mi: Backdoor
  • Doku Doku no Mi: Virulence
  • Doru Doru no Mi: Wick
  • Goe Goe no Mi: Broken Focus
  • Gura Gura no Mi: Aftershock
  • Hana Hana no Mi: Bloom Crusher, Clutch Lock
  • Hiso Hiso no Mi: Call of the Wild, Eavesdrop
  • Horo Horo no Mi: Ghost Legion, Phantom Payload
  • Horu Horu no Mi: Hell Wink, Iron Constitution
  • Kachi Kachi no Mi: Scalding Steam, Friction Burn
  • Karu Karu no Mi: Karmic Return
  • Kilo Kilo no Mi: Weight Shift
  • Kira Kira no Mi: Brilliant Meteor, Unscratchable
  • Kobu Kobu no Mi: Never Surrender
  • Kuku Kuku no Mi: Gourmet Metabolism
  • Mero Mero no Mi: Enthralling Gaze, Heart Rebound
  • Mini Mini no Mi: Lilliput Crush, Tiny Titan
  • Nagi Nagi no Mi: Soundless Step, Dead Air
  • Netsu Netsu no Mi: Melting Point, Scorching Fist
  • Noro Noro no Mi: Noroma Field
  • Ope Ope no Mi: Anesthesia, Puncture Wille - with K-Room and Shock Wille, the awakening now runs the whole canon sequence
  • Ori Ori no Mi: Iron Tether, Bound Hands
  • Oto Oto no Mi: Grand Finale, On the Beat
  • Pero Pero no Mi: Sugar Shell, Sugar Coffin
  • Sabi Sabi no Mi: Collapse, Oxidized Plate
  • Sube Sube no Mi: Frictionless
  • Sui Sui no Mi: Undertow, Breach
  • Suke Suke no Mi: Unseen
  • Supa Supa no Mi: Razor Cyclone, Steel Riposte
  • Yami Yami no Mi: Singularity
  • Yomi Yomi no Mi: Soul Reap, Undying Soul
  • Zushi Zushi no Mi: Deadweight

Zoan

Every awakened Zoan's second form used to have no ability of its own; each one now does.

  • Hito Hito no Mi: Insight, Adaptive Mind
  • Hito Hito no Mi: Daibutsu: Sanctuary
  • Kame Kame no Mi: Snapping Jaw
  • Ryu Ryu no Mi: Allosaurus: Apex Pursuit
  • Ryu Ryu no Mi: Brachiosaurus: Neck Catapult
  • Ryu Ryu no Mi: Pteranodon: Downdraft
  • Sai Sai no Mi: Juggernaut
  • Sara Sara no Mi: Axolotl: Toxic Reserve, Toxic Bloom
  • Tori Tori no Mi: Phoenix: Rebirth Blaze
  • Ushi Ushi no Mi: Bison: Thundering Herd
  • Ushi Ushi no Mi: Giraffe: Neck Hammer
  • Zou Zou no Mi: Trunk Geyser
  • Zou Zou no Mi: Mammoth: Drought Siphon, Ancient Hide
A Few Highlights
  • Trunk Geyser (Zou): a jet of seawater. A Devil Fruit user it soaks loses their powers for a moment, as if they had fallen into the sea
  • Rebirth Blaze (Phoenix): the phoenix burns, untouchable, and is reborn at full health - the health it takes back erupts as a nova. The lower it was, the bigger the blast
  • Thundering Herd (Bison): run a route, and a phantom stampede thunders down the whole of it
  • Ancient Hide (Mammoth): in an awakened form, no single blow takes more than 15% of your health
  • On the Beat (Oto): blows landed on the tempo build a damage combo
  • Anesthesia (Ope): a numbed target's invulnerability frames stop protecting it from you and your side
Changes Renamed abilities

Awakened abilities no longer borrow the names of techniques the manga gives to the fruit's normal form:

  • Entei → Crown of Flames, and Entei Flight → Crown Flight (Mera Mera)
  • Hiraishin → Stormstep (Goro Goro)
  • Kirimanjaro → Longneck Ram (Ushi Ushi: Giraffe)
  • Punk Corrida → Scrap Tempest (Jiki Jiki)
  • Takamagahara → Lightfall Domain (Pika Pika)
  • Yomi no Fubuki → Soulchill Aura (Yomi Yomi)
Reworked awakenings

Every awakening that already existed was revisited when its fruit was extended. Among the larger changes:

  • Damage raised across many abilities that were weaker than the fruit's own base kit - for example Drought Calamity, Ivory Catastrophe, Ao no Rakka, Horn Drill, Ancient Spine Saw and Slick Disarm
  • Mechanics that were promised and missing now work: Ivory Catastrophe actually spins, Candle World burns those caught in its soft wax, Spin (Kame) blocks attacks, Battlefield Resonance applies its bonuses, Kenzan World can no longer be dodged by crouching
  • Friend and foe sorted out: several zones no longer help enemies or hurt allies (Spring Domain, Waterpool Domain, Resonating World, High-Frequency Wall, Kenzan World)
  • Fiddle Overdrive (Bison): no longer knocks you unconscious when it ends, and its steam finally shows
  • Tooltips: many abilities now show their real numbers - heals, durations, cooldowns and bonuses that were missing
  • Every ability description rewritten in the base mod's register
  • Status effect icons redrawn as 18x18 pixel art, matching vanilla's
Sounds
  • Dozens of abilities that were silent now have their own sounds
  • Zone charge sounds no longer play two or three copies of themselves on top of each other
Fixes
  • Interrupted charges (water, Seastone, handcuffs) no longer deliver the ability at full power, and no longer leave you rooted or a zone half-built
  • Spring Domain: allies' jumps are no longer worse inside the field, bounces never lose their speed, and the zone costs a fraction of what it did
  • Spring Fajin: charging in mid-air holds you in place instead of dropping you
  • Drought Calamity: the charge animation no longer breaks in a released game, and the drought no longer drains caves deep under the field
  • Beta Beta mucus no longer slows the server down the more of it exists
  • Dislocated limbs hide correctly when both arms and legs are dislocated
  • Awakening smoke sits on the neck of several forms that had it misplaced
Requirements
  • Minecraft 1.20.1

⚠️ AkumaLib update required: 2.2.0

Just replace the AkumaLib jar in your mods folder with the new one.

Every Zoan awakening is now complete. The awakened Zoans only covered one of their two forms. This release adds the twelve missing awakened forms, gives the Daibutsu its first real ability, and brings the mod to 70 fruits and 148 awakened abilities.

New Content Fruits Abilities
  • Hito Hito no Mi: Daibutsu: Added Nyorai Shinshō
Awakened Zoan Forms

Each awakened Zoan now has both of its forms, not just one. Every new form has its own model, stats and icon, and follows the same calibration as the awakened form the fruit already had.

  • Walk Points: Leopard, Allosaurus, Axolotl, Bison, Giraffe and Sai
  • Guard Points: Kame, Brachiosaurus, Mammoth and Zou
  • Fly Points: Phoenix and Pteranodon
Nyorai Shinshō

The Daibutsu awakening used to be just a form. Nyorai Shinshō brings the palm of the Buddha down from the sky onto the point you aim at, up to 64 blocks away:

  • 120 damage to everything within 14 blocks of the impact
  • Everything it lands on is sealed into the ground for 40 seconds, unable to walk, swim or jump
  • Where the base Impact Blast strikes forward from the fist, this one comes from above, at range, and holds
Quality of Life
  • Your fruit's own abilities work in the new forms: every base ability that needs a Walk, Guard or Fly Point also accepts its awakened version. Kame Rideable, Brachio Bomber, Ancient Sweep, Mammoth Trample, Fujiazami and Flames of Regeneration included
  • Faster flight: the awakened Fly Points use the fruit's normal flight, only faster
  • Awakened Kame Guard Point: crouching retracts into the shell, where almost nothing gets through
  • Awakening smoke: on the new forms, the smoke around the neck follows the model's head
Changes
  • Glittering Storm (Kira Kira): the diamond tornado is no longer put out by rain. Water still stops it
Fixes
  • Titan Trample (Deka Deka), Spin (Kame Kame) and Brachio Stomp (Ryu Ryu: Brachiosaurus) no longer damage their own user
Requirements
  • Minecraft 1.20.1
  • Forge 47.4.18+
  • Mine Mine no Mi 1.20.1-0.11.5
  • AkumaLib 2.2.0 — update required
  • (Recommended) Mine Mine no Mi: Awaken Path for survival progression

Released 2026-09-03 · Download

⚠️ New required dependency: AkumaLib

From this version on, AkumaLib must be installed alongside this mod. Without it the game will stop on Forge's missing-dependency screen.

AkumaLib is a library that adds no content of its own — it holds the shared framework this mod is built on. Just drop it in your mods folder.

Every Devil Fruit in Mine Mine no Mi now has at least one awakening. This release adds 10 new fruits and 34 new abilities, taking the mod to 70 fruits and 135 awakened abilities.

The Logia jumped from 3 fruits to 10.

New Content Fruits Abilities
  • Goro Goro no Mi: Added Kami no Kuni, Hiraishin and Storm Sovereign
  • Pika Pika no Mi: Added Takamagahara, Kousoku and Sun's Blessing
  • Suna Suna no Mi: Added Sabaku no Okoku, Sabaku no Sousou and Kawaki
  • Moku Moku no Mi: Added White Night, White Ash and White Plague
  • Yuki Yuki no Mi: Added Yukiro, Gokkan and Kanpa
  • Gasu Gasu no Mi: Added Taiki, Asshuku and Chuwa
  • Yami Yami no Mi: Added Kyomu and Gluttony
  • Jiki Jiki no Mi: Added Assign World, Punk Corrida and Ferrous Dominion
  • Wara Wara no Mi: Added Harvest of Fate, Nail of Fate and Shared Fate
  • Zushi Zushi no Mi: Added Ukiyo and Zenith
  • Kage Kage no Mi: Added Shadow Marionette and Sunless Brand
  • Hie Hie no Mi: Added Hyosai and Hyoten
  • Magu Magu no Mi: Added Kagutsuchi and Netsuryo
Passive Abilities

Ten of the new abilities are passives — they work on their own, with no key to press, and grow stronger the more you play to the fruit's strengths.

  • Storm Sovereign (Goro Goro): stronger during a thunderstorm
  • Sun's Blessing (Pika Pika): stronger in bright light
  • Kawaki (Suna Suna): stronger standing on sand and quicksand
  • Ferrous Dominion (Jiki Jiki): stronger standing on your own scrap field
  • Zenith (Zushi Zushi): stronger the higher above the ground you are
  • Hyoten (Hie Hie): stronger the more enemies around you are frozen
  • Netsuryo (Magu Magu): banks heat from molten ground, spent by Kagutsuchi
  • Gluttony (Yami Yami): scales with the blocks you have swallowed
  • White Plague (Moku Moku), Kanpa (Yuki Yuki), Shared Fate (Wara Wara), Sunless Brand (Kage Kage): each extends its fruit's own loop
Quality of Life
  • Animations: charged abilities now play a wind-up pose, so an attack can be seen coming
  • Sounds: new sound effects across the Moku, Yuki, Gasu, Suna, Hie and Magu kits
Fixes
  • Ability descriptions: 18 abilities showed a raw translation key instead of their description, and 46 more had text that no longer matched what the ability did
  • Performance: fixed a lag source that ran on every block face on every chunk rebuild, caused by the invisible block system
  • Icons: reworked the Suke Suke no Mi icons, and redrawn Kousoku

docs.title: Awaken Path
docs.text:
Mine Mine no Mi: Awaken Path gives Mine Mine no Mi a survival progression for Devil Fruit awakenings. A player's fruit awakens on its own once they are strong enough and have kept it long enough; no command needed.

Version documented 2.2.0 Mod id mineminenomiawakenpath Download CurseForge Changelog Every release

It adds no abilities of its own: it decides when a fruit awakens. What an awakened fruit can do comes from the base mod and from addons such as Awaken Awaken no Mi, whose awakened abilities unlock the moment the fruit awakens.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Mod Version Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge 47.4.18 or later Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.x

AkumaLib is not needed.

docs.title: How a fruit awakens
docs.text:
With the default settings, a player's fruit awakens once both conditions hold:

Condition Default Details Doriki the base mod's maximum Doriki The base mod's Doriki Limit option, 10,000 by default. A fixed threshold can be set instead. Time with the fruit one real day (1,728,000 ticks) Only time spent online with the current fruit counts. Time logged out does not.

Each condition can be switched off in the configuration. With only one of them on, that one alone decides; with both off, no fruit awakens through this mod.

docs.title: When it is checked
docs.text: The mod checks a player whenever they gain Doriki, eat a Devil Fruit or log in, and once a minute while they play. A fruit that is already awakened is not checked again.

docs.title: The time counter
docs.text:
• It starts at zero when a fruit is eaten.
  • It is kept through death.
  • It is cleared when the player loses their fruit, so a new fruit starts from zero.
  • A player who already had a fruit before Awaken Path was installed gets a counter at their next login, starting from zero.

docs.title: The awakening
docs.text:
When a fruit awakens, the player gets, each part of which can be turned off:

  • a title on screen, Awakening, with the subtitle "The fruit's true power stirs within you..." (in French for a French game: Éveil);
  • a sound;
  • a burst of particles around them.

The base mod then grants the awakened fruit's abilities straight away.

Awakenings are switched on for you

The base mod has an Enable Awakenings option, off by default, in each world's serverconfig/mineminenomi-server.toml. Awaken Path turns it on, whatever that file says, unless you switch off its Force Enable Awakenings setting.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Every setting, its default and the exact file content are on the Configuration page.

Released 2026-06-07 · Download

Fix a related server issue where awakening could not be unlocked, and move were not listed.

Released 2026-05-04 · Download

🆕 What's New

New Awakening Condition: Time Spent With Your Fruit

  • Awakening can now require a minimum amount of playtime with your Devil Fruit
  • Only time spent online is counted — logging off does not progress the timer
  • Fully configurable from 1 hour to several years, with a reference table built directly into the config file
  • Can be disabled independently from the Doriki condition (set to -1 to disable)

Visual & Sound Effects on Awakening

  • 🔊 Sound — A mysterious sound plays upon awakening, heard by all nearby players
  • ✨ Title — A full-screen title and subtitle appear in both English and French
  • 🌟 Particles — END_ROD and SOUL_FIRE_FLAME particles burst around the player
⚙️ Configuration

New [Effects] section in the config file — each effect can be toggled independently:

Option Default Description Awakening Sound true Play a sound on awakening Awakening Title true Show a full-screen title Awakening Particles true Spawn particles around the player

New option in [Unlock]:

Option Default Description Time With Fruit Threshold 1728000 Online ticks required (1,728,000 = 1 real day) 🔧 Fixes & Improvements
  • Timer automatically initialized for players who already had a fruit when updating from v2.0.0
  • Awakening conditions are now checked every in-game minute as a fallback
  • Time counter resets if the player loses their Devil Fruit

Minecraft 1.20.1 — Forge 47.4.18 — Mine Mine no Mi 0.11+

Released 2026-04-05 · Download

⚠️ Breaking Changes
  • Requires Mine Mine no Mi 0.11+ — This version is a full port to Minecraft 1.20.1 and is not compatible with previous versions of the mod or Mine Mine no Mi.
✨ What's New 🔓 Awakenings now enabled by default

Awaken Path now automatically forces the Enable Awakenings option of Mine Mine no Mi to true for every world, without requiring manual configuration of Mine Mine no Mi's config file.

This behaviour is fully configurable via Awaken Path's own config file:

[Unlock]
    # When enabled, forces Mine Mine no Mi's 'Enable Awakenings' option to true,
    # regardless of its config file value.
    # Default: true
    "Force Enable Awakenings" = true

Set it to false to restore Mine Mine no Mi's default behaviour.

✅ Awakening unlock check on Devil Fruit consumption

A new verification is now performed at the moment a player eats a Devil Fruit to determine whether they meet the awakening unlock requirements. This ensures the awakening state is evaluated at the right time in the progression flow.
