docs.title: Advancements
docs.text:
The Inventor tab ("Build, sift and fit parts at the Workshop") holds:

  • Tinkerer's Bench (build a Workshop), Apprentice Inventor (reach Inventor level 5) and Scavenger (find Iron Scrap and Mysterious Parts);
  • salt: Sea Sifter (make a Sieve), Salt of the Sea (sift salt), Finer Grains (make a Fine Sieve);
  • rods: Reel It In (a Reel), Whopper! (a Whopper Fishing Rod), A Rod for a Sea King (the Sea King Fishing Rod);
  • the Upgrade Bench: The Fitting Bench (build one), Rigged (fit a rod part), Fully Rigged (fit both the Fishing Rod Upgrade and the Fishing Line Upgrade on one rod), Man of Steel (fit a Whopper Rod Upgrade);
  • Rock Breaker (an Enhanced Pick-axe);
  • dials: Sky Shell (a Mysterious Dial), Fire in a Shell (a Flame Dial), Ignition (a Jet Dial), A Dial That Listens (a Tone Dial);
  • Blind Spot (a Blind Spot Cannonball);
  • one challenge, Storm in a Shell (a Thunder Dial).

docs.title: Lumberjack
docs.text:
The Lumberjack fells trees that grew in the world and plants saplings. The trade leads to the three great trees: the Kuuigosu, the Burning Tree and, at the top of the trade, the giant Treasure Tree Adam. The Carpenter builds hulls from their woods.

Workstation none: you work in the forest Tools the Woodsman's Axe and the Felling Saw, made by the Inventor Levels 1 to 100; felling the Adam needs level 50

docs.title: Felling for XP
docs.text:
Felling pays per log, by the tree it came from:

Log from XP per log Any other tree (vanilla's, Mine Mine no Mi's…) 1 The fruit trees' woods (Red Fruit, Blue Fruit, Brown Fruit, Horrific Pear, Golden Fruit, Palm) 2 Kuuigosu 3 Burning Tree 4 Treasure Tree Adam 6

The log, the wood block and both stripped forms all count. Planting any sapling pays 1 XP (not in Creative).

Only wood that grew counts.

  • A log a player placed is marked: breaking it again pays nothing and is never doubled, whoever placed it.
  • The log must belong to a standing tree: leaves somewhere along its trunk, or a trunk taller than 24 logs.

docs.title: The tools
docs.text:
Both are made by the Inventor at the Workshop.

  • Woodsman's Axe (Inventor 20: 2 Pure Iron Ore, 3 Diamond Fragments, 2 Mysterious Parts, 2 logs)
    • Diamond tier, 1 800 uses, repaired with Diamond Fragments.
    • Its tooltip reads "A Lumberjack's second log turns up 25% more often": the level-25 perk's 15 % becomes 18.75 %.
    • It hits for less than a diamond axe, on purpose.
  • Felling Saw (Inventor 35: 4 Pure Iron Ore, 3 Mysterious Parts, 2 logs)
    • Iron tier, 1 200 uses, repaired with Pure Iron Ore.
    • Its tooltip reads "One cut brings down the trunk, up to 64 logs". It follows the logs of the same wood that are joined to the cut, diagonals included, upward and outward but never below the cut, and it skips logs a player placed.
    • Each log costs one use, pays its XP, and can be doubled by the level-25 perk.

docs.title: The three great trees
docs.text:
Kuuigosu Burning Tree Treasure Tree Adam Grows wild in Beach, Stony Shore, Mangrove Swamp Badlands, Eroded Badlands, Wooded Badlands, Savanna Plateau, Windswept Savanna Dark Forest, Old Growth Spruce Taiga, Old Growth Pine Taiga How rare about 1 chunk in 22 about 1 chunk in 40 about 1 chunk in 1 600 Shape a straight trunk 6–9 blocks high, round crown a straight trunk 5–7 blocks high, round crown; the leaves glow a giant 68–92 blocks high, a trunk 13 blocks across flaring to 19 at the foot, a crown about 31 across on several branches; the trunk is hollow, with a doorway and a ledge of logs winding up inside Sapling from its leaves 8 % (Fortune: 10 / 12 / 15 %) 8 % (Fortune: 10 / 12 / 15 %) 0.05 % (Fortune: 0.06 / 0.07 / 0.08 %) Planting the sapling Lumberjack 15 Lumberjack 25 Lumberjack 50 Bone meal works works refused; the sapling also grows about 60 times more slowly than a normal one Felling anyone anyone only a Lumberjack of level 50 XP per log 3 4 6
  • They grow wild only where the ground would take their sapling.
  • Only a Lumberjack can plant these three saplings. The fruit trees' saplings can be planted by a Farmer or a Lumberjack.
  • Anyone else who tries to fell the Adam sees "The Adam does not give. Only a Lumberjack of level 50 can fell it." and the block does not break. The lock covers only its log, its wood and their stripped forms: its leaves, its planks and everything made from them are free to anyone.

docs.title: The woods
docs.text:
Cruise adds nine wood sets: the six fruit-tree woods (Red Fruit, Blue Fruit, Brown Fruit, Horrific Pear, Golden Fruit, Palm) and the Lumberjack's three (Kuuigosu, Burning Tree, Adam).

  • Each set has thirteen blocks: Log, Stripped Log, Wood, Stripped Wood, Planks, Slab, Stairs, Fence, Fence Gate, Door, Trapdoor, Button and Pressure Plate. An axe strips the log and the wood as in vanilla.
  • The woodwork recipes are ordinary crafting-table recipes, the same as vanilla's, and belong to no trade: they give no trade XP. Any of a wood's logs gives 4 Planks, 4 Logs give 3 Wood (4 Stripped Logs give 3 Stripped Wood), and the rest follow the usual vanilla patterns.
  • The planks count as ordinary planks in any recipe that takes "any planks".
  • Burning Tree wood never catches fire: it is not flammable and lava does not set it alight. The Burning Tree hull is the fireproof one (see Boats).

This table lists the nine woods and their sets:

Wood Its set Adam 11 crafting recipes: planks, wood, stripped wood, stairs, slab, fence, fence gate, door, trapdoor, button, pressure plate Blue Fruit 11 crafting recipes: planks, wood, stripped wood, stairs, slab, fence, fence gate, door, trapdoor, button, pressure plate Brown Fruit 11 crafting recipes: planks, wood, stripped wood, stairs, slab, fence, fence gate, door, trapdoor, button, pressure plate Burning Tree 11 crafting recipes: planks, wood, stripped wood, stairs, slab, fence, fence gate, door, trapdoor, button, pressure plate Golden Fruit 11 crafting recipes: planks, wood, stripped wood, stairs, slab, fence, fence gate, door, trapdoor, button, pressure plate Horrific Pear 11 crafting recipes: planks, wood, stripped wood, stairs, slab, fence, fence gate, door, trapdoor, button, pressure plate Kuuigosu 11 crafting recipes: planks, wood, stripped wood, stairs, slab, fence, fence gate, door, trapdoor, button, pressure plate Palm 11 crafting recipes: planks, wood, stripped wood, stairs, slab, fence, fence gate, door, trapdoor, button, pressure plate Red Fruit 11 crafting recipes: planks, wood, stripped wood, stairs, slab, fence, fence gate, door, trapdoor, button, pressure plate

The Carpenter builds hulls and lockers from Kuuigosu, Burning Tree and Adam Planks, and Adam Planks also go into the Blacksmith's Kuro Kabuto.

docs.title: Level perks
docs.text:
Level Perk What it does 10 "Logs give 50% faster under your axe" ×1.5 breaking speed on logs 25 "15% chance a felled log gives two" a log from a natural tree drops twice (18.75 % with the Woodsman's Axe) 40 "Leaves you break drop saplings twice as often" the leaves roll their drops a second time, and only the saplings are kept

Level 50 brings no perk but a lock: only a Lumberjack of level 50 can fell the Treasure Tree Adam.

docs.title: Advancements
docs.text: The Lumberjack tab opens at Lumberjack level 1: Apprentice Lumberjack (level 5), Three Woods (hold a Kuuigosu Log and a Burning Tree Log), and the challenge The Tree That Cannot Be Chopped Down (fell the Treasure Tree Adam: getting an Adam Log is enough), which rewards 100 experience points.

docs.title: Merchant
docs.text:
The Merchant makes nothing and gathers nothing: they sell, and learn by selling. Every Belly they earn from Cruise's travelling merchants, from their contracts and at the Auction House counts toward their level. They are also the only ones who can read the torn treasure maps that turn up in chests, on stalls and on the end of a fishing line.

Workstation none: the travelling merchants and the Auction House Advancements tab Trade Levels 1 to 100; torn maps up to level 75

You only earn Merchant XP if you practise the Merchant trade (in Crew mode, if it is your trade). A player who does not can still sell, deliver contracts and use the Auction House, but gets none of the Merchant's XP, prices or bonuses, and cannot read a torn map.

docs.title: How a Merchant earns XP
docs.text: Source XP Selling goods to a Cruise merchant (the Sell window) 1 XP per 10 Belly of the sale (at least 1) Delivering a merchant's contract 1 XP per 10 Belly of the reward (at least 1) One of your lots selling at the Auction House 1 XP per 10 Belly of its price (at least 1); if you are offline, it is given when you log in or collect Being the first to open a buried treasure chest Rumor map 100 XP, Old map 400 XP, Legendary map 1 200 XP

docs.title: Selling to the travelling merchants
docs.text:
Five travelling merchants visit the Overworld: the Fishmonger, the Hunting Merchant, the Travelling Cook, the Prospector and the Materials Trader. Each buys the goods of one trade through a Sell window, keeps a stall and brings three contracts.

A Merchant sells to them on better terms:

  • from level 1, everything you sell pays +0.5 % per level, up to +25 % at level 50, where the bonus stops growing;
  • from level 10, the market fills up half as fast with what you sell;
  • from level 25, you pay 15 % less for what you buy from them (a village cured of its fever gives 20 % to those who helped: you keep the better of the two, not both);
  • from level 40, a merchant's purse no longer limits what he buys from you (your own Belly cap still does).

Who comes where and when, and what each one buys and for how much: see Merchants and contracts.

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text:
Every merchant arrives with three contracts for goods of his own trade. They pay 1.5 to 1.8 times what he would pay over the counter, not out of his purse, and your price bonus raises the reward too.

From level 10, merchants also show you the third contract, the one they keep for Merchants: it always pays the top premium (×1.8), and half the time adds a Torn Old Map. See Merchants and contracts.

docs.title: The Auction House
docs.text:
The Auction House is one market for the whole server, where players list lots for each other. A Merchant has it easier with every level:

  • the listing fee falls by 1.5 % of itself per level, down to a quarter of the normal fee at level 50 (2 % becomes 0.5 % with the default fee);
  • +1 lot you may have up every 5 levels;
  • +1 day a lot stays up every 2 levels;
  • from level 1, the price history: what a kind of good has sold for lately, on average.

The fee stops falling at level 50; the extra lots and days keep growing up to level 100.

docs.title: Treasure maps
docs.text: Only a Merchant can decipher a torn treasure map: a Torn Rumor Map from level 1, a Torn Old Map from level 20, a Torn Legendary Map from level 75. The map then leads to a buried chest, and the first player to open it earns the grade's Merchant XP. See Treasure hunts.

docs.title: Level perks
docs.text:
Level Perk What it does 1+ "Sales and contracts with Cruise's merchants: +…%" +0.5 % per level on everything you sell to a Cruise merchant and on every contract reward, up to +25 % at level 50 (no more after that) 1+ "Auction House: fee -…%, +… lots up, +… days up, the prices' history" a lower listing fee (down to a quarter at level 50), +1 lot every 5 levels, +1 day every 2 levels, and the average recent price of each kind of good 10 "The market fills half as fast with what you sell" you can sell twice as many of one kind (32 instead of 16) before its price halves 10 "Merchants show you the contract they keep for Merchants" you see, and can deliver, each merchant's third contract 25 "15% off Cruise merchants' stalls" 15 % off everything you buy from a Cruise merchant; the Buy screen still shows the full price, but you are charged less. Not on Mine Mine no Mi's own traders 40 "A merchant's purse no longer limits what he buys from you" a merchant buys everything you bring, whatever is left in his purse (your own Belly cap still applies)

The professions book shows the two level-1 perks with their current values, so they grow as you level.

docs.title: Advancements
docs.text: The Trade tab opens at Merchant level 1: Trade (become a Merchant), Apprentice Merchant (level 5), A Deal Is a Deal (deliver a merchant's contract), Going Once, Going Twice (sell a lot at the Auction House), X Marks the Spot (dig up a treasure) and Legendary Treasure (dig up the treasure of a legendary map).

docs.title: Miner
docs.text:
The Miner earns XP by breaking ore and certain rocks. As the trade grows, the rock starts to give up finds on top of its normal drops: Diamond Fragments, Marble, Kairoseki, Dial Fragments, Pure Iron Ore and more. At the Masonry, the Miner turns those finds into marble blocks, iron and diamonds.

Workstation Masonry How it is made 8 Stone around a Crafting Table Tools any pickaxe of the right tier; the Enhanced Pick-axe is made by the Inventor Levels 1 to 100; new finds up to level 50

docs.title: What counts
docs.text:
• The block must be broken in Survival, with a tool that would normally harvest it (a pickaxe of the right tier for an ore).
  • Silk Touch turns the trade off: a block taken whole gives no XP and no finds.
  • The Explosive Rock and Mine Mine no Mi's dials specifically need a pickaxe.

docs.title: XP from breaking
docs.text:
Ores pay Miner XP at any level: the rarer the ore, the more it pays, and Ancient Debris pays the most. Plain Deepslate, Tuff, Calcite and Diorite pay nothing of their own; they only pay when a find turns up. Each find that drops pays its own extra XP on top.

This table gives the XP each block pays when broken:

Breaking XP any coal ores 2 any copper ores 2 Nether Quartz Ore 2 any iron ores 4 any redstone ores 4 any gold ores 6 any lapis ores 6 Kairoseki Ore, Deepslate Kairoseki Ore 10 any diamond ores 12 any emerald ores 12 Ancient Debris 20

docs.title: Finds in the rock
docs.text:
From Miner level 5, some blocks can turn up finds as well as their normal drops.

  • Each find is rolled separately every time the block is broken, so a block with several possible finds can give more than one at once.
  • Each find starts at a set Miner level; the professions book lists it as an unlock at the lowest level where it appears.
  • A player who does not practise the Miner trade gets no finds at all.

This table lists every find, the block it comes from, its chance, the Miner level it needs and the extra XP it pays:

Breaking Can turn up Chance Level XP Explosive Rock Explosive Rock Fragment 100 % 5 6 any diamond ores Diamond Fragment 30 % 5 4 Axe Dial, Breath Dial, Eisen Dial, Flame Dial, Flash Dial, Impact Dial, Milky Dial, Reject Dial Dial Fragment 100 % 10 10 Calcite Marble 8 % 10 6 Diorite Marble 4 % 10 6 Kairoseki Ore, Deepslate Kairoseki Ore Kairoseki 25 % 15 4 any iron ores Iron Scrap 12 % 18 8 any iron ores Pure Iron Ore 10 % 25 8 any coal ores Explosive Rock Fragment 8 % 28 10 Deepslate Diamond Fragment 0.4 % 35 15 Deepslate, Tuff Mysterious Parts 0.3 % 38 16 Kairoseki Ore, Deepslate Kairoseki Ore Dense Kairoseki 10 % 42 20 any iron ores Pure Iron Ore 15 % 45 8 Ancient Debris Netherite Scrap 25 % 46 25 Deepslate, Tuff Kairoseki 0.15 % 50 30

Two finds are worth a closer look:

  • Pure Iron Ore from iron ores has two separate rolls: one from level 25 and a second one from level 45, on top of the first.
  • Mysterious Parts (from level 38) and Kairoseki (from level 50) can turn up in plain Deepslate and Tuff, very rarely.

docs.title: The Explosive Rock
docs.text:
Red, cracked boulders two to three blocks across, half buried, found in badlands, desert and mountain biomes (in roughly one chunk in five there).

  • A Miner of level 5 or more who breaks one with a pickaxe gets 1 to 3 Explosive Rock Fragments. About 12 % of the time, a Rock Lizard was hiding inside.
  • Anyone else sets it off: a small blast that hurts but breaks no blocks, and leaves them nothing.

docs.title: Dials
docs.text: From Miner 10, breaking one of Mine Mine no Mi's dials (Axe, Breath, Eisen, Flame, Flash, Impact, Milky or Reject Dial) with a pickaxe shatters it into 2 to 4 Dial Fragments, instead of the dial itself. Below level 10, the dial breaks and drops as normal.

docs.title: Marble
docs.text: There is no marble ore: Marble only comes from breaking Calcite (8 %) and Diorite (4 %), from Miner 10.

docs.title: The Enhanced Pick-axe
docs.text:
The Enhanced Pick-axe is made by the Inventor at the Workshop (Inventor 25: 5 Diamond Fragments, 3 Mysterious Parts, 1 log).

  • Diamond's mining tier, 1 800 uses, repaired with Diamond Fragments.
  • Its tooltip reads "A Miner's finds turn up 25% more often". This adds up with the level-10 perk, for ×1.875 in all.

docs.title: The Masonry
docs.text:
The Masonry is the Miner's workstation; it needs a pickaxe to be picked back up. Every recipe asks for a Miner level and pays Miner XP.

It turns Marble into building blocks (Marble Block, Marble Slab, Marble Stairs, Polished Marble and Polished Marble Slab), Pure Iron Ore into Iron Ingots, and Diamond Fragments into a Diamond. All marble blocks need at least a stone pickaxe to drop.

These are the Masonry's recipes:

Makes Level XP Ingredients Marble Block 1 12 4 × Marble Marble Slab ×6 5 20 3 × Marble Block Marble Stairs ×4 8 26 3 × Marble Block Polished Marble ×4 14 38 4 × Marble Block Polished Marble Slab ×6 16 42 3 × Polished Marble Iron Ingot ×2 30 70 Pure Iron Ore Diamond 44 98 9 × Diamond Fragment

docs.title: Where the finds go
docs.text:
• Explosive Rock Fragments become Gunpowder for the Chemist.
  • Dial Fragments become the Mysterious Dial and the Jet Dial for the Inventor.
  • Pure Iron Ore goes into the Inventor's Magnet, Woodsman's Axe, Felling Saw and Hull Ram, the Carpenter's Adam boats, the Blacksmith's Warabide Sword and several Tailor pieces.
  • Kairoseki and Dense Kairoseki feed the Blacksmith's sea-stone weapons and handcuffs.

docs.title: Level perks
docs.text: Level Perk What it does 10 "Finds in the rock turn up 50% more often" every find's chance ×1.5 (never above 100 %) 25 "10% chance an ore gives its drops twice" one ore in ten gives its normal drops a second time 40 "20% chance an ore gives its drops twice" replaces the 10 %

docs.title: Advancements
docs.text: The Miner tab opens at Miner level 1: Apprentice Miner (level 5), Diamond in the Rough (find a Diamond Fragment), Carved in Stone (find Marble), Sea-Prism Stone (mine Kairoseki), Handle With Care (break an Explosive Rock into fragments) and Shell Shock (shatter a dial into Dial Fragments).

docs.title: Musician
docs.text:
The Musician writes scores at the Music Stand and plays them on an instrument for their crew. A tune gives every crewmate within reach a buff that lasts 20 minutes or more: speed, faster work, healing, attack, armour, luck, more XP or more Doriki. It is the one trade whose recipes already run to level 100.

Workstation Music Stand How it is made crafting table, no level: Paper, a Note Block, Sticks Instruments made by the Inventor at the Workshop Levels 1 to 100; scores up to level 100 XP writing scores (10 + 2 × the recipe's level) and playing them

docs.title: The Music Stand
docs.text:
You build the Music Stand at an ordinary crafting table. Anyone can build one:

Top Middle Bottom Paper, Note Block, Paper —, Stick, — Stick, —, Stick

It faces you when you place it.

docs.title: Writing scores
docs.text:
Every score takes 2 Paper, plus the tune's own ingredient (listed under The eleven tunes):

Tier Ink Tune's ingredient Extra I an Ink Sac 1 — II an Ink Sac 2 2 Gold Nuggets III a Glow Ink Sac 3 a Gold Ingot and a Diamond Fragment

Scores stack to 16; tier II scores are uncommon, and tier III scores are rare and shine.

docs.title: Playing a tune
docs.text:
1. Carry an instrument. You do not need to hold it: the best instrument anywhere in your inventory plays. "Best" means the one that reaches furthest, then the one whose tune lasts longest.

    Instrument Tune reaches Tune lasts Uses Bamboo Flute 8 blocks 20 minutes 32 Fine Bamboo Flute 10 blocks 25 minutes 48 Master's Bamboo Flute 12 blocks 30 minutes 64 Violin 12 blocks 25 minutes 64 Fine Violin 15 blocks 30 minutes 96 Master's Violin 18 blocks 35 minutes 128 Guitar 16 blocks 30 minutes 128 Fine Guitar 20 blocks 35 minutes 192 Master's Guitar 24 blocks 40 minutes 256

    The Fine and Master's ones are the Inventor's improvements of the plain ones: gilded, the Master's in black lacquer. Seated at a grand piano, you play the piano instead, whatever you carry.

  2. Hold use with the score in hand. You play for 3 seconds, standing. Notes rise around you and the instrument sounds the tune's motif.

  3. When the tune ends:
    • you and every member of your crew within reach get the tune's buff for the instrument's duration. "Crew" means your Mine Mine no Mi pirate crew: nobody outside it gets anything, however close, and a player with no crew plays for themselves alone;
    • the score is used up;
    • the instrument loses one use.

Your crewmates see "<you> plays <tune> for the crew".

To play, you need:

  • to practise the Musician trade ("Only a Musician can play a score" in Crew mode);
  • a Musician level at least the score's level ("This tune takes a Musician of level N");
  • an instrument ("You need an instrument to play it").

One tune at a time. A new tune replaces the last. Tunes are separate from meal buffs and remedies, so a tune stays alongside a Cook's Appetite.

docs.title: The grand piano
docs.text:
The Inventor builds the Grand Piano (level 40), then a Fine one (level 70) and a Master's one (level 100). It carries further and lasts longer than anything you can carry:

Piano Tune reaches Tune lasts Grand Piano 20 blocks 35 minutes Fine Grand Piano 30 blocks 45 minutes Master's Grand Piano 40 blocks 60 minutes
  • Placing it: it takes 2 × 4 blocks, its stool included, and they must all be free. The block you aim at becomes the left half of the stool; the keys, the body and the tail run away from you.
  • Playing it: right-click the piano to sit down at it, then use a score as usual. Only one player sits at a piano at a time ("Someone is already playing this piano").
  • A piano is never worn out: it has no uses to lose.
  • Break any part of it and the whole piano comes back as one item.

Like any instrument, the piano plays for you and your crew within reach: set it on your ship's deck, and the crew aboard hears it.

Every tune has three tiers, each its own score. The buff shows as I, II or III.

docs.title: The lost tunes
docs.text:
Four more tunes are not learned by level. Their recipe has to be found first: a Score Recipe, read once (right-click) by anyone who practises the Musician trade, teaches it for good. Until then, the profession page shows the tune as "Find its recipe", and the Music Stand refuses it.

Tune Musician level Ingredients (with 2 Paper and an Ink Sac) Effect Moonlight Serenade 10 2 Glowstone Dust night vision Laboon's Song 20 a Sea King Scale breathe under water Binks' Sake 40 2 Ancient Rice harmful effects wear off twice as fast Drums of Liberation 60 2 Leather and a Gold Ingot +15 % attack speed and +50 % knockback resistance

A lost tune has one tier only: its score shines like a tier III one, and its effect lasts and reaches as far as the instrument says.

Where the Score Recipes are found (the rarer the tune, the rarer its recipe: out of 10 recipes, 4 Moonlight Serenades, 3 Laboon's Songs, 2 Binks' Sakes, 1 Drums of Liberation):

  • Chests: 8 % of shipwreck supply and treasure chests, underwater ruins, buried treasure, dungeons, village cartographers' and woodland mansions' chests; 25 % of Mine Mine no Mi's richest chests (the large pirate ship's treasure, the medium pirate ship's captain, the Marine battleship's treasure, the Marine bases' captains, the bandit fort's secret stash, the ghost ship's captain, the caravans).
  • Merchants' stalls: 8 % of the travelling merchants' stalls, 35 % of the Ship Merchant's (Events at sea). Prices: 800, 1 500, 4 000 and 9 000 Belly.
  • Contracts: 4 % of public contracts, 10 % of the contract kept for Merchants; the Ship Merchant's big orders bring one 30 % of the time (50 % for the Merchant's).

docs.title: Musician XP
docs.text:
You earn XP two ways:

  • Writing scores at the Music Stand: each score pays 10 + 2 × its level (see The recipes).
  • Playing: each performance pays 10 + the score's level + 10 for each crewmate who heard it (up to 8 crewmates).
  • On the stage of a concert: the tune is for every player within reach, the villagers who came to listen count as listeners (up to 16), and the performance pays twice that.

docs.title: Advancements
docs.text: The Music tab ("Play for your crew: become a Musician") holds Apprentice Musician (Musician level 5), First Performance (play a tune) and one challenge, Full House (play a tune for three of your crew or more).

docs.title: Navigator
docs.text:
The Navigator learns by discovering places: every chunk they have never been in, and every new land and new kind of place in their Log Book. At their bench, the Chart Table, they make the tools that find the way: the Log Pose, the Barometer, the Sea Chart and the Eternal Pose. At the helm, they make the Carpenter's boats go a little faster.

Workstation Chart Table Advancements tab Navigation Levels 1 to 100; new kinds of land and place open up to level 100

docs.title: The Chart Table
docs.text:
Made at a crafting table from paper, a compass and planks (any kind):

Paper Compass Paper Planks Planks Planks Planks Planks

It faces you when placed and is mined with an axe. The Navigator's four recipes are made there.

docs.title: Charting recipes
docs.text: Makes Level XP Ingredients Log Pose 1 12 Compass, Glass Pane, Leather, Gold Nugget Barometer 20 50 Glass Bottle, 2 × Copper Ingot, Tempest Mouse, Redstone Dust Sea Chart 30 70 2 × Paper, Compass, Pumpkin Octopus Eternal Pose 50 110 Log Pose, Lens, Magnet, 2 × Gold Ingot

docs.title: Exploring
docs.text: A Navigator earns 2 XP for every chunk they have never been in, on foot, by boat or in the air, in any dimension. Going back over old ground pays nothing.

docs.title: The Log Book
docs.text:
Open it with the Log Book button on the Navigator's page of the professions book. It has two sections, filled for any player in the Overworld:

  • Lands: every Overworld biome you stand in (+25 Navigator XP for each new one).
  • Places: every kind of structure you stand in or come within 8 blocks of, from vanilla, Mine Mine no Mi and other mods, except buried treasure (+50 Navigator XP for each new one).

The book also keeps the names of the villages you have been to.

Each tenth of a section you complete pays Belly to anyone, and XP to a Navigator: from 500 Belly and 50 XP at 10 % up to 100 000 Belly and 6 000 XP at 100 %. See Bestiary and Log Book.

docs.title: Level 1: the Log Pose
docs.text:
The Log Pose (does not stack) is a needle under glass that points, like a compass, to the nearest biome of a chosen kind.

  • Use it to switch to the next kind of land your Navigator level opens: it searches and points to the nearest one ("Log Pose set on Forests: N blocks").
  • Use it crouching to search again for the same kind from where you stand.
  • It searches 2 400 blocks around (4 800 from Navigator level 25), with a 3-second cooldown.
  • Only a Navigator can set it; anyone can follow the needle.
Kind of land Navigator level Forests, Beaches, Plains 1 Deserts, Savannas, Taigas 10 Jungles, Swamps, Badlands 20 Mountains, Snowy lands 30 Dark Forests, Cherry Groves 40 Mushroom Fields 60 Ice Spikes 80 the Deep Dark (searched underground) 100

Deserts, Swamps, Plains, Snowy lands and Mushroom Fields also include other mods' biomes of the same kind.

docs.title: Level 20: the Barometer
docs.text:
The Barometer (does not stack) tells anyone who uses it what the weather will do, in real minutes:

  • "Fair weather, set for about N minutes"
  • "Clear for now - rain in about N minutes"
  • "Raining - it clears in about N minutes"
  • "Raining - a storm breaks in about N minutes"
  • "Storm - it passes in about N minutes"

Where there is no sky (the Nether, the End) the needle does not move. It only forecasts the weather; it does not change it.

docs.title: Level 30: the Sea Chart
docs.text:
The Sea Chart (stacks to 16) is a blank chart.

  • Use it to pick the next kind of place your level opens; use it crouching to draw it.
  • It becomes a map ("Sea Chart: Villages") with the nearest such place marked: ocean monuments and woodland mansions with their vanilla icons, the rest with an X. It searches up to 1 600 blocks around.
  • Like a cartographer's map, a chart never leads to a place already charted in the world.
  • The Villages kind leads to Cruise's own villages first, the nearest not yet charted and still lived in, and to one of Minecraft's villages when there is none in reach. The chart takes a few seconds to draw; the game does not stop meanwhile.
  • Drawing uses one blank chart, gives 20 Navigator XP, and has a 3-second cooldown.
  • Only a Navigator can draw one; anyone can read, sell or give the drawn map.
Kind of place Navigator level What it finds Villages, Shipwrecks, Ocean Ruins, Pirate Ships, Training Grounds 30 villages, shipwrecks, ocean ruins; Mine Mine no Mi's small and medium pirate ships, its ghost ship and its training structures Marine Posts, Bandit Hideouts, Pillager Outposts, Temples 40 Mine Mine no Mi's small Marine bases, watch towers and bandit structures; pillager outposts; desert and jungle pyramids Ruined Portals, Witch Huts, Igloos, Trail Ruins 50 the vanilla structures Marine Fortresses, Warships, Ocean Monuments 60 Mine Mine no Mi's large Marine base and large ships; ocean monuments Sky Islands 70 Mine Mine no Mi's sky islands Woodland Mansions 80 the vanilla structure Ancient Cities 90 the vanilla structure Strongholds 100 the vanilla structure

docs.title: Level 50: the Eternal Pose
docs.text:
The Eternal Pose (stacks to 16, uncommon) points to one place, for good.

  • A Navigator uses a blank one to calibrate it where they stand (it takes one from the stack; +40 Navigator XP). From then on it points there and cannot be set again.
  • It is named after the place: the structure they stood in (within 8 blocks), otherwise the biome, or whatever name an anvil gave it.
  • Anyone can use a calibrated one to see how far away the place is ("It points to X: N blocks away", or "in another world").

docs.title: At the helm
docs.text: From level 10, the Carpenter's boats you steer go 1 % faster, on any water; from level 40, 2 % faster (replacing the 1 %). The boat's total speed boost (hull, shape, sail and helmsman together) is capped at ×1.075, so a Navigator makes an ordinary boat faster but adds little to the fastest one. See Boats and the Carpenter.

docs.text: Source XP A chunk never visited 2 A new land in the Log Book 25 A new kind of place in the Log Book 50 Drawing a Sea Chart 20 Calibrating an Eternal Pose 40 Chart Table recipes 12 / 50 / 70 / 110 Each tenth of a Log Book section 50 up to 6 000

docs.text: Level Perk What it does 10 "Fair wind: the Carpenter's boats you steer make a little more way, on any water" the Carpenter's boats you steer go 1 % faster 25 "Long sight: your Log Pose reaches twice as far" your Log Pose searches 4 800 blocks instead of 2 400 40 "Trade winds: the boats you steer make more way again" the boats you steer go 2 % faster (replacing the 1 %), within the ×1.075 cap

docs.title: Advancements
docs.text: The Navigation tab opens at Navigator level 1: Navigation (become a Navigator), Apprentice Navigator (level 5), Which Way? (make a Log Pose), Storm Warning (make a Barometer), Charting the Seas (make a Sea Chart), A Way Home (make an Eternal Pose), The Whole World (every land in the Log Book) and Every Port of Call (every kind of place in the Log Book).

docs.title: Tailor
docs.text:
The Tailor sews Mine Mine no Mi's clothing at the Sewing Table: hats, capes, masks, glasses and characters' outfits, which the base mod ships but never lets players make. The Tailor also sews the Carpenter's boat sails and makes two materials of their own.

Workstation Sewing Table How it is made String, any Wool, Shears on top; 3 planks in the middle; plank, empty, plank at the bottom Recipes 103 Levels 1 to 100; new recipes up to level 50

Every recipe asks for a Tailor level and pays Tailor XP: 12 XP at level 1, rising to 110 at level 50.

docs.title: What the Sewing Table makes
docs.text:
• The Tailor's own materials:
    • Scrap of Cloak (level 1: 2 wool and 1 String give 2).
    • Mask Fragment (level 14: 3 Clay Balls and 1 Yellow Dye).
    • They go into the Bandana (level 1) and the Sogeking Mask (level 29).
  • Boat sails for the Carpenter's boats: the Boat Sail (12), the Fine Sail (28) and the Master's Sail (44). Each better sail is sewn from the one before. See Boats.
  • Base-mod items taken from the crafting table: the Flag (1), the Umbrella (4) and the Medic Bag (8). While the takeOverBaseRecipes setting is on (the default), they are made only here; see the takeover on the Blacksmith page and Configuration.
  • Uniforms and headwear: pirate and Marine uniforms (3 and 4), the Tricorne (6), Sniper Goggles (10), the Wizard Hat (12), the Plume Hat (15), the Bicorne (18), the Wide Brim Hat (20), the Pirate and Marine Captain Capes (22), the MH5 Gas Mask (24), the CP9 outfit (38), the Vice Admiral outfit (45) and the Fleet Admiral's Hat (50).
  • The Straw Hat crew: the Straw Hat (2), Luffy's (7), Zoro's (8), Usopp's (9) and Sanji's (11) outfits, the two Chopper's Hats (26 and 27), the Sogeking Mask (29), Franky's Glasses and Shirt (34) and the Soul King Crown (41).
  • Other characters' outfits and accessories, from level 13 up: pieces for Kuro, Kuroobi, Arlong, Smoker, Mr 1, Mr 3, Mr 5, Crocodile, Kizaru, Law, Senor Pink, Killer, Kuma, Doflamingo and Mihawk, Ace's and Sabo's hats, and more.

The recipes are spread fairly evenly up to level 50 (24 at levels 1–10, 22 at 11–20, 23 at 21–30, 19 at 31–40, 15 at 41–50).

docs.title: Ingredients from the other trades
docs.text:
Besides wool of many colours, string and leather, the recipes call on the whole crew:

  • the Hunter's catches: hides (lizards, frogs, the A Class Toad, the Mole), wings (butterflies, moths, the Flying Penguin), fireflies, and the Rock Lizard;
  • the Fisher's fish (Forked-Tail Killifish, Shark, Missile Manta Ray), and Sea King Scales and Fins;
  • the Farmer's Ancient Rice and Medicinal Herb;
  • the Miner's Pure Iron Ore, Diamond Fragments and Explosive Rock Fragments;
  • Iron Scrap, Mysterious Parts, and powders such as Thunder Powder and Flame Powder;
  • Mine Mine no Mi's Cola, and a Seagull for the Fleet Admiral's Hat.

docs.title: InoFruits
docs.text:
InoFruits adds brand-new Devil Fruits to Mine Mine no Mi: fruits the base mod does not have, each with its own abilities.

Version documented 3.3.0 Mod id inofruits Download CurseForge Changelog Every release

docs.title: What it adds
docs.text:
34 Devil Fruits: 4 Logia, 18 Paramecia and 12 Zoan (one of them Mythical), with their abilities, morphs, projectiles and status effects.

The fruits behave like the base mod's own:

  • they drop from the base mod's Devil Fruit boxes, each in the box matching its tier, and are drawn as often as a base mod fruit;
  • the base mod's one-fruit-per-world rule applies to them unchanged;
  • they appear in the base mod's Devil Fruits creative tab.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Mod Version Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge 47.4.18 or later Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.x (built against 1.20.1-0.11.5) AkumaLib 3.0.0 or later

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
1. Install Forge for Minecraft 1.20.1, then put Mine Mine no Mi, AkumaLib and InoFruits in your mods folder.
  2. Find a fruit in a Devil Fruit box. Wooden, iron and golden boxes each hold the fruits of their tier, listed in Fruits.
  3. Eat it. Its abilities appear in the base mod's ability menu, grouped under the fruit.

Upgrading from before 3.0.0

The ferret fruit was renamed Ita Ita no Mi, Model: Ferret in 3.0.0. Older saves are remapped automatically: the fruit, its abilities and its forms carry over.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Every InoFruits release for Minecraft 1.20.1, newest first, as published on CurseForge.

docs.title: 3.3.0Devil Fruit boxesNew looksRenamedFixes
docs.text:
Released 2026-09-30 · Download

The Iro Iro no Mi becomes the Some Some no Mi, the ferret gets three more coats, and fruits renamed in 3.0.0 come back in old worlds. The fruits are also put in the Devil Fruit boxes by data files now, so a modpack or a server can choose which box gives which fruit.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 3.0.0 or newer.

⚠️ Update AkumaLib to 3.0.0 first. With an older AkumaLib the game refuses to start and says which version it needs. And with AkumaLib 3.0.0, InoFruits 3.2.0 or older puts its fruits in no box: update both together.

  • Every fruit is in the same box as before, as common as a Mine Mine no Mi fruit of its tier, and the chance for a box to give a fruit of the tier above still reaches them.
  • Modpacks and servers can change it with a data pack: move a fruit to another box, make it rarer or more common, or take it out (see AkumaLib's Devil Fruit boxes page).
  • Three more coats for the ferret: albino, polecat and full black, in both forms. The ferret now comes in six coats, and each player still always gets the same one. ⚠️ With more coats to choose from, about half the players' ferrets change colour once.
  • The Iro Iro no Mi is now the Some Some no Mi ("dye"): the old name belongs to a fruit of One Piece itself. Nothing to do: a fruit you have eaten, its abilities, and the fruits in your chests and inventories carry over under the new name.
  • Fruits renamed in 3.0.0 carry over. A world last played before 3.0.0 now keeps, under their new names, the fruits in its chests and inventories and the fruit each player had eaten; they used to vanish. (A world already opened with 3.0.0 or later lost them then, and they cannot come back.)
  • The ferret's body no longer floats above its legs in its animal form, at rest and when it walks.
  • The unicorn needs a form for its horn techniques. Horn Thrust, Prism Lance, Unicorn Charge, Starfall, Guiding Light, Moonlight Burst, Purify and Sanctuary no longer work in human form.
  • The mosquito walks. Its six legs now move when it walks on the ground instead of sliding.
  • Hybrid forms move with your techniques. When a technique moves your arms (Saigoppe, a punch...), the fur, claws or armour the form puts on them now follow instead of staying behind.

Released 2026-09-27 · Download

Nine transformations redrawn, three coats for the ferret, clearer ability tooltips, and a large fix pass. Ability tooltips now say what kind of damage a technique deals and what it goes through, the first-person view of every hybrid form matches what others see, and more than thirty bugs are gone.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.9.0 or newer.

⚠️ Update AkumaLib to 2.9.0 first. With an older AkumaLib the game refuses to start and says which version it needs. Existing worlds and servers need nothing else.

New looks
  • Redrawn transformations: Kani Kani (both forms), Mushi Mushi, Kero Kero, Zuku Zuku and Wani Wani, then Ita Ita, Isa Isa, Nezu Nezu and Usa Usa (both forms each).
  • The ferret comes in three coats: cinnamon, champagne and silver. Each player always gets the same one, in both forms.
  • The rat is bigger, in both forms.
  • The hare's back kick follows its new body: it gathers its legs, then throws both of them out behind.
Clearer tooltips
  • Every ability shows the kind of damage it deals, with Mine Mine no Mi's own icons: slash, blunt, projectile, fire, poison, light and so on, and which kind of Haki can boost it.
  • Where Mine Mine no Mi has no icon (wind, honey, indirect hits…), the tooltip says it in words, for example "Source Wind, Indirect".
  • Abilities that go through armour or through a Logia's intangibility say so ("Pierces Armour, Logia").
  • Abilities whose damage was missing from the tooltip now show it: Blood Spear, Blood Rush, Blood Festival, Blood Drain, Hoppu, and Shio no Wa's damage against the undead.
  • Damage from the fruits now counts as ability damage everywhere (Kugi Yoroi, Toge, Fuusen, Blood Shell), with the right death messages. Ekibyo's sickness is now poison. Two Oki Oki laws have their own death messages: "struck back by the law" and "healed to death".
First person
  • Hybrid forms show their arm in the right place. The fur, claws or armour drawn over the player's hand could be shifted, and the hand showed past the ferret's claws, especially after crouching.
  • Hone Hone and Neji Neji show the player's hand again, under the bones or the drill. Fugu Fugu, Suji Suji, Wani Wani and Wata Wata now show on the arm what they show in third person.
  • Black Leg users see their leg, as others see it: the hare's or frog's leg, or the player's own leg with the paws, hoof, nails or fibres the form puts on it. It used to show the bare arm.
  • Auras show on the player's own hand and leg in hybrid forms (Armament Haki, Diable Jambe…).
Fixes

Duplications and loot - Taking items from a Bai Bai clone with Te Kobo duplicated them. - Oatari multiplied ancient debris (and other blocks that drop themselves) without limit, and paid its bonus even when the block was not broken. - Tsuribito never actually doubled a catch.

Allies are spared - Kohaku, Mitsu Goromo, the golem's Nomikomi, Kugi nails and Kugi Ame, Blood Spear and Mitsu Suberi's honey trail no longer hit, trap or slow crewmates.

Transformations and space - Many transformations suffocated when crouching under a low ceiling. - Wani Wani's walk form and Kani Kani's guard form suffocated in the low gaps they are made to fit. - Ichi Ichi could teleport creatures into walls.

Zones and dimensions - Placed zones and the Kaze Kaze tornado followed their user into another dimension. - A Kabe wall survived a dimension change, and its end could remove another player's dirt. - Oki Oki: No Escape kept pulling people back to a spot outside the zone after it moved.

Abilities - Tatsumaki hurt creatures twice. Taiatari's blast could add damage on top of the hit. - Horn blows wiped out absorption hearts gained during the blow (from a totem, for example). - Oki Oki: Grounded did not ground flight such as the unicorn's or the Phoenix's. - The Alicorn passive kept refusing harmful effects while it should have been off (Seastone, Silence). - Ikusa Gesho, Anshi and Hige removed the player's own potion effects. - Nejikomi gave permanent fall protection, and bored blocks vanished when the inventory was full. - Silent Soles muted the footsteps of everyone next to the user. - Mushi Mushi's stealth stayed off as long as the last creature hit was alive. - Hasai and Choyaku removed any root on the Suji Suji user, even one put there by someone else. - Ten projectiles had no name in death messages. - The game could start with an AkumaLib or Forge version that then crashed.

Released 2026-09-25 · Download

Six new Devil Fruits, eleven new abilities for existing fruits, and a balance pass. The addon goes from twenty-eight fruits to thirty-four, including its first Mythical Zoan.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.6.0 or newer.

⚠️ Update AkumaLib to 2.6.0 first. With an older AkumaLib the game refuses to start and says which version it needs. Existing worlds and servers need nothing else.

New fruits Zoan Uma Uma no Mi, Model: Unicorn: the unicorn

Mythical Zoan · golden box · 13 abilities

A Mythical Zoan on par with the base mod's Phoenix, and a healer as much as a fighter. The unicorn flies in both forms, leaving a rainbow behind it, and a crewmate can ride on its back.

The horn is the whole kit. Horn Thrust and Prism Lance go through armour, absorption and even a Logia's intangibility. Unicorn Charge runs through a line of enemies, Starfall calls five lances of light down on a spot, and Guiding Light draws a target to the user, an enemy to hit or a crewmate out of danger. On the other side, Purify and Sanctuary wash harmful effects away and keep new ones off the user and their allies. Moonlight Burst does both at once: the unicorn rears up, blasts enemies away and heals everyone on its side.

The Alicorn passive holds the horn's light: it burns away harmful effects as they land (hard control excepted) and heals the user while transformed. Horn blows refill it.

Kuma Kuma no Mi, Model: Grizzly: the grizzly bear

Zoan · iron box · 8 abilities

A brawler. A hybrid with huge clawed arms, or a whole grizzly on four legs. Claw Swipe knocks away everything in front, Salmon Swipe flips one target into the air, Maul charges and pins the first enemy it meets to the ground, and Roar slows and weakens everyone nearby while mobs run.

Two passives while transformed: Fury hits harder the more the bear is hurt (a gauge shows the bonus), and Thick Fur softens melee blows, resists knockback and keeps the cold out.

Paramecia Chi Chi no Mi: blood

Paramecia · golden box · 9 abilities

The user pays with their own blood and takes it back from others. Every technique costs blood. The Blood Reserve gauge fills with the blood the user loses and pays before their health does. A cost never kills.

Blood Spear, Blood Rush and Blood Pool make enemies bleed. Blood Tether pulls a bleeding enemy in (or drags a crewmate out of danger), and Blood Drain takes the blood back from everyone bleeding nearby to heal the user. Blood Shell clots into a thick shell that shatters on the enemies around it if it breaks. Blood Bond takes half the damage the crew suffers. And once the gauge is half full, Blood Festival spends all of it in a burst of spikes that hits harder the lower the user's health.

Oki Oki no Mi: law

Paramecia · golden box · 16 abilities

The user declares a law, and everyone around obeys it, the user included. Sixteen laws, one in force at a time, proclaimed in the chat of the players nearby: Halt, Grounded, Levitate, Truce, Ceasefire, Silence (no Devil Fruit powers), No Healing, No Escape, Disarm, No Haki, Reveal, Retribution (every blow comes back to its giver), Inversion (every heal hurts), Blindness, No Building and Walk.

The zone follows the user. Its size can be changed in the settings (32 blocks by default). The fruit wins by choosing the rule that hurts the other side more than it hurts you.

Kugi Kugi no Mi: nails

Paramecia · wooden box · 6 abilities

Nails that pin rather than kill. Kugizuke throws a big nail that roots the target, Kugibari fans small nails (three of them pin), and Kugi Ame rains nails on a spot. Kugi Yoroi makes nails stand out of the user's whole body, hurting whoever strikes or touches them. Kugi Dome nails the user's own feet down to hold their ground. Kuginuki rips every nail out of every body nearby, and the more nails, the more it hurts.

Kutsu Kutsu no Mi: shoes

Paramecia · wooden box · 7 abilities

Six pairs of soles, one worn at a time, drawn on the user's feet. Water Soles walk on water and lava, Wall Soles climb walls and hang from ceilings, Silent Soles make no sound and keep mobs from noticing, Weighted Soles cancel knockback, Spring Soles jump about seven blocks high with no fall damage, and Skate Soles glide fast on any ground. Stomp throws up everyone around, and hits harder in Weighted Soles.

New abilities for existing fruits
  • Kaze Kaze no Mi: Kyuin. The air reverses in front of the user and drags every enemy in a wide cone towards them.
  • Shio Shio no Mi: Shio Bashira. A pillar of salt that holds the target in place for 3 seconds and stops it healing for 10.
  • Shio Shio no Mi: Dassui. Draws the water out of every enemy around the user: they are hurt, slowed, salted and pulled slightly closer.
  • Tsuchi Tsuchi no Mi: Ryusa. Quicksand where the user looks, dragging enemies to its centre and wearing them down.
  • Tsuchi Tsuchi no Mi: Jisuberi. A landslide in front of the user that hurts, knocks away and briefly buries every enemy in a wide cone. Both new Tsuchi abilities have a bigger version, Dai-Ryusa and Dai-Jisuberi, while the earth golem is up.
  • Gamu Gamu no Mi: Hanekaeshi. A sheet of gum in the air that bounces every projectile back at whoever threw it.
  • Kane Kane no Mi: Zeni Nage. Flicks a golden coin at the target for 1 berry a throw. The luckier the user, the harder it hits.
  • Kane Kane no Mi: Oatari. For 30 seconds, creatures the user kills drop more loot and the ores they mine drop twice.
  • Kiza Kiza no Mi: Kiza Maki. Puts a slider on every enemy in a wide cone at once.
  • Kiza Kiza no Mi: Zen Hikisage. Pulls every slider around down at once: marked bodies lose both speed and strength, and the user takes a share of each.
  • Kiza Kiza no Mi: Oshiage. The user lowers their own slider to raise a marked ally's: they lose speed or strength, and the ally gains it.
Balance
  • Kaze Kaze no Mi hits harder. Oroshi, Kamaitachi and Tatsumaki deal more damage (Oroshi and Kamaitachi about 60% more).
  • Shio Shio no Mi hits harder. Kessho no Yari, Shio Barai and Shio no Ame deal about 50% more, and Shio no Wa hurts the undead more.
  • Tsuchi Tsuchi no Mi hits harder. Jibashiri and Tsubute deal more damage, in and out of the golem.
  • Mushi Mushi no Mi: Kyuketsu bites harder and stores a fixed amount of blood per bite.
  • Zuku Zuku no Mi: Kazakiribane's feathers deal twice as much damage. Washizukami carries its target for 8 seconds instead of 15.
  • Gamu Gamu no Mi: Fuusen's bubble bursts harder.
  • Mitsu Mitsu no Mi: Mitsu Suberi and Mitsu Numa deal twice as much damage. Mitsu Goromo is shorter (6 seconds instead of 8), slows less and has a longer cooldown.
Fixes
  • Kyuketsu and Nejikiri could hit a crewmate standing in front of the user instead of the enemy behind. Single-target attacks now only pick enemies.

Released 2026-09-25 · Download

A crash fix and redrawn fruit icons. No fruit, ability or balance changes. Existing worlds and servers need nothing special.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.4.0 or newer, the same as 3.0.0.

Fixes
  • The Kero Kero no Mi's tongue crashed the game. Tobitsuki crashed as soon as the tongue hit a block or a creature, and Shita as soon as it caught a creature. Both now work as described: Tobitsuki sticks to a block or a body and pulls the frog to it, and Shita catches its target.
Changes
  • All 28 fruit icons have been redrawn. Each fruit keeps its shape and colours, with a brighter look and a green stem like the base mod's fruits, so they sit better next to them in your inventory.

Released 2026-09-18 · Download

Thirteen new Devil Fruits and 80 new abilities. The addon goes from fifteen fruits to twenty-eight, and from 77 abilities to 157.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.4.0.

⚠️ AkumaLib 2.4.0 is required, not optional. 2.1.0 to 2.3.0 lack the classes this release uses (pulls, rendered lines, block protection), and the game crashes the first time one of them is needed. On a server, the server and every client must run the same AkumaLib: its network protocol changed, and mismatched versions refuse to connect.

⚠️ Three fruits from 2.0.0 were renamed, and some abilities need the fruit eaten again. Read Breaking changes, below the new fruits, before updating a world.

New fruits Logia Kaze Kaze no Mi — wind

Tier 3 · golden box · 9 abilities

The addon's largest kit, and a Logia built around moving people before hurting them. Toppu blows everything in front away, Josho lifts whatever stands in a column of rising air up to eighteen blocks, and the next two presses make it pay: Oroshi slams everything airborne within twelve blocks back into the ground, and Shippu turns the user into wind that rushes through a line of enemies.

Around that: Kamaitachi, a spinning disc of air that flies dead straight; Fuuheki, a wall of wind that deflects every projectile coming within four blocks; and Tatsumaki, a tornado that follows wherever the user looks. Rain does not stop it. Water still does. The user flies, faster outside of combat.

Paramecia Suji Suji no Mi — muscle

Tier 2 · iron box · 5 abilities

Three forms, each growing muscle somewhere different. The upper body hits extremely hard and very slowly, the legs run faster and jump higher without hitting any harder, and the full body does a bit of both, less well than either. Hasai punches out a shockwave that goes through enemies and walls; Choyaku jumps a long way and lands on whatever is underneath.

Mitsu Mitsu no Mi — honey

Tier 2 · iron box · 6 abilities

Almost no damage in the whole kit, and that is the design. Everything here decides where a fight happens: a pool of honey that slows anything standing in it (the user included), a coat that slows a target's movement and attacks, and Kohaku, honey that hardens into amber and locks a body in place for three seconds. Amahada coats the user so that anyone hitting them gets stuck, Mitsu Gusuri heals over time, and Mitsu Suberi slides on honey, leaving a sticky trail behind.

Gamu Gamu no Mi — chewing gum

Tier 2 · iron box · 5 abilities

A control kit with four verbs: root, shove, float, pull. Neba Dan sticks a target in place, Fuusen blows a bubble that drifts and pops on contact, Kikyu inflates a balloon that lets the user float down from any height, and Banji Gamu shoots a strand of gum up to thirty blocks and reels in whatever it catches, drawn as a real stretching strand. The passive glues the user's feet to walls and ceilings.

Neji Neji no Mi — twist

Tier 1 · wooden box · 5 abilities

Both forearms become spinning drills. Its signature is penetration: Rasen is the only technique in the addon that does not stop at the first body in its path, and drills a line through everything in front of the user. Nejikiri wrings one target off its feet, Totsushin charges drills first through a crowd, and Nejikomi tunnels through the ground and leaves the hole behind. It respects protected areas, like the base mod's own Mogu Mogu no Mi.

The drill arms are grafted onto the player's own body, so the hitbox does not change.

Wata Wata no Mi — cotton

Tier 1 · wooden box · 5 abilities

Cotton armour over the chest, shoulders and arms that softens hits and falls, a cloud that blinds anyone inside it and hides the user, and a packed ball of cotton that picks up whatever it hits and carries it off. Watazumi turns some of the user's cotton into white wool.

⚠️ The fruit has a drawback you cannot switch off: while the cotton armour is on, the user takes more damage from fire.

Kiza Kiza no Mi — the gauge

Tier 1 · wooden box · 3 abilities

No damage anywhere, and nothing created. Kiza Dashi puts a slider on a target, Hikisage pulls that slider down and hands the user whatever it took off, and Kiza Modoshi pulls back the user's own sliders, clearing every bad effect on them at once. Alone, the fruit can do nothing but cleanse. In front of one opponent, everything it takes, the user gains.

Kane Kane no Mi — treasure

Tier 1 · wooden box · 4 abilities

A fruit with no combat line at all, on purpose. Komyaku highlights everything valuable within thirty-two blocks, through walls. Meate marks the single most valuable thing within sixty-four blocks for two minutes. Nakami shows what is inside a container without opening it. And the passive keeps the user lucky: Devil Fruit boxes they open upgrade three times as often.

Zoan Mushi Mushi no Mi, Model: Mosquito

Tier 2 · iron box · 8 abilities

The addon's first form that is allowed to be bad at everything. The mosquito is weaker than a plain player on every line of the stat screen, and what pays for it is not on that screen: the smallest hitbox in the addon, and hostile mobs that do not bother targeting it. Both forms fly.

Kyuketsu drinks from whatever is in front of the user and heals them, and keeps part of that blood in a sac shown as a gauge. The blood slowly goes bad, and Chibukure spends all of it at once for a heal and a burst of speed. Kabashira raises a column of mosquitoes around the user that bites everything inside: the fruit's only answer to more than one opponent.

Kero Kero no Mi, Model: Frog

Tier 2 · iron box · 7 abilities

Light, vertical and immune to fall damage: the opposite of the crocodile it shares the water with. Its tongue does three things: Shita pulls a target in and holds it, Shita Muchi whips without pulling, and Tobitsuki sticks to a block or a body and pulls the frog to it. Hoppu jumps and slams whatever is underneath. Nendeki makes the skin sticky, and the next projectile of any kind that hits the user sticks harmlessly instead.

Fugu Fugu no Mi, Model: Pufferfish

Tier 1 · wooden box · 7 abilities

A defensive Zoan whose full form is too round for most doors. Bocho puffs the user into a spiky ball that shoves everything nearby away, Togeuchi fires a ring of spines in every direction, and Hosui blows a jet of air that throws the user backwards, out of trouble.

Two passives do the real work while a form is on: melee attackers take part of the blow back, and poison goes both ways, onto anyone the user hits and anyone who hits them.

Usa Usa no Mi, Model: Hare

Tier 1 · wooden box · 5 abilities

The addon's only evasion kit. The hare outruns anything on the ground and jumps far higher than a player, and Ushiro Geri, a two-legged kick that launches the target one way and the hare the other, is the hardest single hit in the wooden tier. It pays for all of it by being fragile: its two forms carry the lowest armour in the addon.

Kani Kani no Mi, Model: Crab

Tier 1 · wooden box · 4 abilities

A crab that breathes underwater and walks on the sea floor in its full form, and grows a shell and two pincers in its hybrid, where it is slow and hard to push around. Yokobashiri is a dash with no wind-up (sideways, in the shell), and Hasamikomi catches whatever is in front of the user in a claw and drags it along.

⚠️ Breaking changes — read before updating a world Three fruits and their forms have new ids

Six fruits were renamed during this cycle so that every root is two morae, the way the base mod names its own. Only three of them existed in 2.0.0, so only these three affect an existing world:

2.0.0 3.0.0 Itachi Itachi no Mi, Model: Ferret Ita Ita no Mi, Model: Ferret Fukuro Fukuro no Mi, Model: Owl Zuku Zuku no Mi, Model: Owl Kujira Kujira no Mi, Model: Whale Isa Isa no Mi, Model: Whale

Their ids changed with their names, along with the forms and abilities that carried the old root:

Kind 2.0.0 id 3.0.0 id Fruit inofruits:itachi_itachi_no_mi_model_ferret inofruits:ita_ita_no_mi_model_ferret Fruit inofruits:fukuro_fukuro_no_mi_model_owl inofruits:zuku_zuku_no_mi_model_owl Fruit inofruits:kujira_kujira_no_mi_model_whale inofruits:isa_isa_no_mi_model_whale Ability ferret_walk_point ita_ita_walk_point Ability ferret_heavy_point ita_ita_heavy_point Ability fukuro_fukuro_fly_point zuku_zuku_fly_point Ability fukuro_fukuro_assault_point zuku_zuku_assault_point Ability fukuro_fukuro_flight zuku_zuku_flight Ability kujira_kujira_walk_point isa_isa_guard_point — also renamed, see below Ability kujira_kujira_heavy_point isa_isa_heavy_point Ability kujira_rideable isa_rideable Morph ferret_walk, ferret_heavy ita_ita_walk, ita_ita_heavy Morph fukuro_fukuro_fly, fukuro_fukuro_assault zuku_zuku_fly, zuku_zuku_assault Morph kujira_kujira_walk, kujira_kujira_heavy isa_isa_guard, isa_isa_heavy

Ferret Dart keeps its id. The ferret's two forms now read Ita Ita Walk Point and Ita Ita Heavy Point, like every other Zoan in the addon.

The whale's full form is now a Guard Point. The base mod calls a defensive Zoan's full form a Guard Point (Zou, Mammoth, Brachiosaurus, Kame), and the whale is the addon's tank. The form is the same; only its name and id changed.

What carries over

The addon maps every old id to its new one when an older world loads, so:

  • fruits already in chests, inventories and item frames become the renamed fruits;
  • the forms and their effects resolve under their new ids.

Tested on a world created with 2.0.0: fruits in storage and players who had already eaten the ferret, owl or whale come through the update with their fruit and forms under the new names. If a form or an ability is still missing for someone, run /ability reset <player> and have them eat the fruit again.

Abilities added to fruits that were already out

Mine Mine no Mi grants a fruit's abilities when the fruit is eaten and never checks the fruit again. A player who already has one of these fruits will not see the new abilities until they run /ability reset <player> and eat the fruit again:

Fruit New in 3.0.0 Isa Isa no Mi (whale) Shiofuki, Utagoe Wani Wani no Mi Lunging Bite, Belly Crawl Nezu Nezu no Mi Hassho Chiku Chiku no Mi Chikuken Bai Bai no Mi Baizo The loot files are gone

The addon no longer ships loot_modifiers or loot_tables/dfboxes files. Its fruits are now added straight into Mine Mine no Mi's own Devil Fruit box pool, at the same weight as the base mod's fruits of the same tier. A datapack that overrode inofruits:loot_modifiers/* or inofruits:dfboxes/*_additions no longer does anything. To tune the rates, edit the base mod's box tables instead.

Changes to existing fruits New abilities
  • Wani Wani no Mi — Lunging Bite and Belly Crawl. Death Roll sat behind the crocodile's slowest form with no way to get in range. Lunging Bite throws the whole body a few blocks forward and ends on the first enemy in the way, further and harder in the full form. Belly Crawl slides the user in low and fast, and the next bite that lands hits harder. Death Roll also gets its own sound.
  • Isa Isa no Mi — Shiofuki and Utagoe. The whale finally has something to do while crowded: Shiofuki erupts a column of water in front of it that launches enemies into the air and puts out fires on everyone caught in it. Utagoe is a song that makes the user and nearby allies resist damage. Both reach further in the full form.
  • Nezu Nezu no Mi — Hassho. The rat's plague used to be something to watch spread. Hassho sets off every plague on nearby carriers at once, each taking all the damage its plague had left.
  • Chiku Chiku no Mi — Chikuken. A third way to spend the battery: the next punch carries all the stored force into one target. The most dangerous way to carry a charge, and the kit's highest single hit.
  • Bai Bai no Mi — Baizo. Every clone next to the user splits again, up to a limit. The Bai Bai no Mi is complete at three abilities.
Look and feel
  • Animations across every fruit, on the techniques where a pose helps, and the Zoans' full forms move with them: the crocodile rolls around its own spine, the crab's pincer snaps, the pufferfish holds its puff, the whale lands with a splat.
  • The Wani Wani no Mi's Heavy Point has a new model. The crocodile head replaces the player's, and the player's own body stays visible under osteoderms, a tail and claws. Its hitbox is smaller to match.
  • Sounds where they were missing: Bone Throw, Weasel Bound, Washizukami, and a generated wind for Tatsumaki and insect hum for Kabashira. Saigoppe's spray is replaced by a softer puff.
  • The Tsuri Tsuri no Mi's fishing line is drawn as a real line instead of a trail of particles.
  • The Kobo Kobo no Mi shows what it hits. Two of its techniques reach eight blocks and used to show nothing at all; they now leave particles, so the player can see what they hit.
  • New fruit sprites for the ferret, the owl, the whale and the Tsuchi Tsuchi no Mi, and ability icons redrawn without the dark outline the base mod's icons do not have.
  • Every ability description is rewritten to read like the base mod's: one short sentence saying what the technique does.
Fixes
  • Kajiru could gnaw open chests. The rat's bite only checked for claimed areas, so in the wild it could eat a chest, barrel, furnace, spawner or redstone component and spill its contents. It now follows the base mod's own block-protection list, which only allows terrain, building blocks, foliage and ore.
  • Hako Kobo emptied containers with griefing turned off. Spilling a container now counts as griefing, and respects the ability-griefing config and, for a mob caster, the mobGriefing rule.
  • Kabe's wall ignored the base mod's placement rules. It now goes through them like the base mod's own barriers do: griefing settings, challenge arena bounds, restricted blocks and restoring areas.
  • Ichi Ichi and Tsuri Tsuri ignored the protection whitelist at the target. A technique the server whitelisted was allowed where the caster stood and refused where the target stood.
  • Marks and side effects landed on hits that did nothing, such as a strike on an intangible Logia or an invulnerable body, and vanished on hits that did land whenever someone else had struck the same target a moment earlier. Both are fixed across the addon.
  • In randomized fruits mode, this addon's fruits showed their real icon under a "Generic Fruit" label, which gave them away. They are now disguised like every other fruit.
Under the hood

More of what this addon used to carry itself now comes from AkumaLib: pulling a body toward the user, lines drawn between two points, protected-area checks, and the way a Devil Fruit box picks up this addon's fruits. None of it is visible in game; all of it is why AkumaLib 2.4.0 is required.

How they fit into Mine Mine no Mi
  • They drop from its own Devil Fruit boxes, wooden, iron and golden, now as entries in the box's own pool at the same weight as the base mod's fruits of the same tier. Finding one is exactly as rare as finding any other fruit of its tier.
  • Both 2.0.0 limitations are gone. This addon's fruits now come out of the 5% tier cascade like the base mod's, and no box is held under its intended chance any more.
  • They appear in its Devil Fruits creative tab, and take part in randomized fruits mode.
  • They are calibrated against its kits, not above them.
  • The encyclopaedia, fruit shifting and "eat a fruit you already have" all pick them up unchanged.

Released 2026-09-10 · Download

Nine new Devil Fruits and 45 new abilities. The addon goes from six fruits to fifteen, and from 32 abilities to 77.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.1.0.

⚠️ AkumaLib 2.1.0 is required, not optional. 2.0.0 does not contain what this release compiles against, and loading against it fails during registration rather than gracefully.

New fruits Logia Tsuchi Tsuchi no Mi — earth

Tier 3 · golden box · 7 abilities

The first Logia whose element is everywhere, and its balance is a data file rather than a number. Every other Logia's Travel is bounded by its substance being rare — sand, ice, glass — so the earth tag deliberately stops at the dirt family: the user phases through the top layer of the world and stops the moment they go below it or step into a building. Stone is a wall, and that is the fruit's counter-play.

A wave along the ground, a temporary wall that takes itself back down, an immobilisation that does no harm at all and is the strongest thing in the kit, and one thrown mass. Over all of it, a golem form that grows every technique it holds — including their range, which is the axis such forms usually forget.

Yuge Yuge no Mi — steam

Tier 2 · iron box · 7 abilities

The only fruit in the game that carries water — the universal Devil Fruit weakness — to somebody standing on dry land. A soaked target loses their own fruit's powers for a moment, and every technique here is priced twice: once against a dry body, once against one the fruit has already soaked. It is the addon's first kit that always wants two presses.

Scalding damage doubles on a soaked body; the finisher is worth five times as much and uses the mark up. Around that: a lunge that soaks what it passes through, and a vent that lifts the user ten blocks and holds them there while the column below scalds whatever stays in it.

Its Logia body is immune to fire but not to lava, and takes half again as much from cold — the trade that pays for the immunity.

Paramecia Bai Bai no Mi — multiplication

Tier 3 · golden box · 2 abilities

The smallest kit in the addon, and deliberately so. What sets its tier is not damage: it can make a permanent copy of an item, which is worth more to a world than any number in this mod. Devil Fruits and containers holding other items are refused in code. The other ability puts three copies of the user on the field.

Both cooldowns are in the config file — this is the fruit a server owner is most likely to have an opinion about.

Ichi Ichi no Mi — swapping

Tier 2 · iron box · 5 abilities

Three techniques and a passive, no damage anywhere, and one idea under all of them: two places trade what is standing in them. Swap with any body still in sight, swap everything in a column twenty blocks across at once — the user included, with no say in where they land — or swap two other things and never move at all.

It is the addon's most lethal fruit without dealing a point of damage, and that is the intent: where somebody ends up is the weapon.

Chiku Chiku no Mi — accumulation

Tier 1 · wooden box · 3 abilities

A battery. It stores the force of every blow the user takes and gives the whole of it back at once — either at one target or at everything within six blocks. The shape comes from the base mod's own Karma, and the divergence is the point: this one only charges on a blow that actually lands.

Tsuri Tsuri no Mi — fishing

Tier 1 · wooden box · 4 abilities

The addon's first fruit that pulls. Everything that displaced anything before this pushed. All four abilities are one line read differently: take a body and bring it here, take a wall and bring the user to it, or bring back every dropped item and scrap of experience within twenty-six blocks.

Zoan Fukuro Fukuro no Mi, Model: Owl

Tier 2 · iron box · 7 abilities

The addon's first fruit that flies. Two forms that genuinely disagree: the owl is fast in the air, hopeless on foot and weightless in a fall; the hybrid hits twice as hard, flies slower and lands like a person. Silent flight, night vision, a grab that carries its target off, a wing beat that clears a room, and a thrown flight feather.

Nezu Nezu no Mi, Model: Rat

Tier 1 · wooden box · 5 abilities

The base mod has no small mammal at all — its smallest Zoan is the axolotl. The ferret beats this fruit on nearly every attribute and the Mogu Mogu keeps digging, so what is left for the rat is the thing neither of them has: a bite that spreads. Nothing else in the base mod or this addon carries an affliction from one body to another on its own.

Kujira Kujira no Mi, Model: Whale

Tier 1 · wooden box · 4 abilities

The addon's first tank, and the first Zoan here whose two forms are a real trade-off rather than a big one and a small one. The Walk Point stops playing and starts absorbing — the heaviest defence in the addon, on a body whose land speed is cut by 90% — while the Heavy Point keeps ordinary mobility and reach. One charge, which reads the form it is used in.

Changes to existing fruits
  • Death Sleep, a recovery hold for the ferret: it drops limp and does not get up. Nothing stops attacking it — it simply takes less, and mends fast while it lies there.
  • The Nezu Nezu no Mi moved to tier 1 during development, which took the iron box back off its chance ceiling. The Yuge Yuge no Mi has since put it back.
  • A new fruit sprite for the Fukuro Fukuro no Mi.
  • Status icons for the five effects that had none — they were drawing the missing-texture square in the HUD.
Fixes
  • Weasel Bound and Tail Sweep damaged their own caster. Both used a sphere that does not exclude the user.
  • Habataki's animation never stopped. The two-argument animation call runs until something calls stop, and a one-shot technique has nothing to call it from — so the wing-beat pose stayed on forever.
  • The paint blob never despawned when it hit a block, and went on flying.
  • The owl's Assault Point drew armour on arms that are wings.
  • canMount() was read backwards on the ferret and the crocodile. It means "may climb onto a vehicle", not "may be ridden" — the two forms could not sit in a boat or on a horse for no reason.
Under the hood

Most of the release's non-fruit work was moving this addon onto AkumaLib rather than keeping its own copies: eleven form gates, ten morph stat blocks, five effects, the targeting helpers and the amplified-presentation plumbing all now come from the library. None of it is visible in game; all of it is why 2.1.0 of the library is required.

How they fit into Mine Mine no Mi

Unchanged from 1.0.0, and worth repeating:

  • They drop from its own Devil Fruit boxes — wooden, iron and golden — so finding one is as rare as finding any other fruit of its tier.
  • They appear in its Devil Fruits creative tab, rather than in a tab of their own.
  • They are calibrated against its kits, not above them.
  • The encyclopaedia, fruit shifting and "eat a fruit you already have" all pick them up unchanged.
Known limitations
  • A fruit from this addon does not drop from the base mod's 5% tier cascade. That nested roll goes through a code path that skips loot modifiers by design, so only the direct box rolls can yield one.
  • The iron box is at its ceiling. With six tier 2 fruits, one roll cannot express the intended chance, so each of them shows up about 7% less often than its share. The wooden box is 20% under for the same reason. Both are deliberate: one chest yielding one fruit is worth more than the exact number.

Released 2026-09-07 · Download

The first release. Six Devil Fruits, 32 abilities, none of them in the base mod.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.0.0.

The fruits Shio Shio no Mi — salt

Logia · golden box · 7 abilities

A control Logia built on purification rather than dehydration. It denies more than it damages: a salted body stops regenerating and takes half of any other healing, a ring of salt sears the dead and strips weak blessings, and the user can come apart into a current of salt and pour through the air.

Hone Hone no Mi — bone

Paramecia · iron box · 6 abilities

Wear your own skeleton on the outside — and while it holds, every other technique in the kit hits harder. Throw a bone that curves back and strikes twice, grow a blade out of your arm, spray splinters, knit yourself back together.

Iro Iro no Mi — paint

Paramecia · wooden box · 5 abilities

Paid for in information and position, not damage. Sixteen colours, and the colour is a real choice: war paint gives a different bonus for each. Blind with a thrown blob, mark a target through walls, or take on the colours behind you — which holds only while you stand perfectly still.

Kobo Kobo no Mi — spill

Paramecia · wooden box · 4 abilities

Takes things away from people rather than taking them apart. Force a target to drop what it holds, empty every container nearby onto the floor at once, or leave everything around you starving.

Itachi Itachi no Mi, Model: Ferret

Zoan · iron box · 6 abilities

Mobility, not muscle. Three times a player's speed, a hitbox short enough to get where nobody else fits, and almost no armour to show for it. Two forms, a bounding leap, claws that leave a bleed, and a musk that leaves everything nearby reeling while the user walks away.

Wani Wani no Mi, Model: Crocodile

Zoan · iron box · 4 abilities

The ferret read backwards: an ambush predator. Slow and armoured on land, twice as fast in the water and able to breathe there. Its death roll takes hold in the jaws and rolls — beast form only, and deadlier in water — and a tail sweep throws everything around it clear.

How they fit into Mine Mine no Mi

Nothing here replaces or rebalances the base mod.

  • They drop from its own Devil Fruit boxes — wooden, iron and golden — so finding one is as rare as finding any other fruit of its tier.
  • They appear in its Devil Fruits creative tab, rather than in a tab of their own.
  • They are calibrated against its kits, not above them. The base mod's own numbers are the ceiling: a new fruit sits beside the Magu Magu and the Gomu Gomu in the same loot pool, so it has no business outclassing them.
  • The encyclopaedia, fruit shifting and "eat a fruit you already have" all pick them up unchanged.
Known limitations
  • A fruit from this addon does not drop from the base mod's 5% tier cascade. That nested roll goes through a code path that skips loot modifiers by design, so only the direct box rolls can yield one.
  • The crocodile's kit is the newest and the shortest; more abilities for it are planned.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Settings live in config/inofruits-common.toml:

Section Setting Default What it does bai_bai_no_mi fukuseiCooldown 6000 (5 min) Cooldown of Fukusei, which makes one permanent copy of the held item. The value that most affects a server's economy. bai_bai_no_mi baiBunshinCooldown 2400 (2 min) Cooldown of Bai Bunshin, which spawns three copies of the user for 30 seconds. bai_bai_no_mi baizoCooldown 1800 (90 s) Cooldown of Baizo, which doubles the clones already standing. bai_bai_no_mi baizoMaxClones 8 Most clones one player may have at once. A server performance limit. yuge_yuge_no_mi kumoriSuppression 60 (3 s) How long Kumori switches off a soaked Devil Fruit user's powers. 0 removes the suppression. oki_oki_no_mi okiRadius 32 blocks Radius of the Oki Oki no Mi's law zone around the user, from 8 to 64. Everyone inside obeys the law in force, the user included. Past about 48 blocks, players no longer see the creatures the law acts on.

Durations are in ticks (20 ticks = 1 second).

Ship the file to your players

The file is not synchronised to clients. The server always enforces its own values, but a player's ability tooltips read their copy. A server that changes a cooldown should give its players the same file, or their tooltips will show the defaults.
