docs.title: Box odds
docs.text:
A Devil Fruit box gives one fruit at most. When it opens:

  • 5% of the time, it also rolls the next box up (wooden → iron → golden), and a fruit from there comes first;
  • 95% of the time, it rolls five fruits from its own list, where every fruit is equally likely;
  • it keeps the first fruit still available: with one fruit per world, a fruit someone already has is skipped.

With every fruit still available, no Luck and only Mine Mine no Mi and InoFruits installed:

Box Fruits in the box Each of its own fruits A fruit from a higher box No fruit Wooden 39 (15 from InoFruits) 2.32% iron 4.52%, golden 0.238% 4.76% Iron 40 (12 from InoFruits) 2.26% golden 4.75% 4.76% Golden 26 (7 from InoFruits) 3.65% — 5.00%

docs.title: What changes the odds
docs.text:
• Luck: each point of the Luck attribute adds 5% to the chance of rolling the next box up, and takes 5% off the chance of rolling fruits. The base mod's New World, once active, counts as one more point.
  • Fruits already found: with one fruit per world, a fruit someone already has is skipped and the box looks further down its five rolls, so the remaining fruits come up more often.
  • Other addons that add fruits to the boxes share the same odds: each new fruit makes every other one of its box a little rarer.

Figures computed from Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5's box logic and the boxes as the game loads them with InoFruits, then checked against 200,000 simulated openings of each box.

The box icons are the Devil Fruit box textures of Mine Mine no Mi, by Wynd and its other authors, shown to identify the boxes. The fruit sprites are InoFruits' own.

docs.title: Sky Island
docs.text:
Mine Mine no Mi: Sky Island adds Skypiea as a dimension of its own to Mine Mine no Mi: the sea of clouds, the Angel Islands and their Skypiean villages, the Upper Yards where the City of Gold was lost, and Weatheria, the weather scientists' floating island. The way up is a Knock-Up Stream erupting from the floor of the deep ocean.

Version documented 0.3.0 (beta) Mod id inosky Download CurseForge · 0.3.0 · changelog

A beta

Worlds are generated from this version's rules. A later version may change what stands in chunks that have not been explored yet.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Mod Version Minecraft 1.20.1 Forge 47 or later Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 AkumaLib 4.0.0 or later

Client and server.

The base mod's sky islands

Mine Mine no Mi's own sky islands no longer generate in the overworld: Skypiea takes their place. Those already generated in an existing world stay where they are.

docs.title: The dimension
docs.text:
Getting there and back the Knock-Up Stream, the arrival, falling back to the overworld Getting around the waver, the Milky Roads between the islands Angel Islands islands of cloud: Skypiean villages, the White Berets, Angel Beach, Heaven's Gate Upper Yards the great islands of earth: the Giant Jack, Shandora, the Shandias and their camps Weatheria the weather scientists' floating island: Haredas, the scientists, weather for sale Wildlife the South Bird, two flying mounts, the Cloud Fox and the Giant Dog; the fish of the cloud sea; the three predators of the Upper Yards Blocks the clouds, the village blocks and the weather cloud in 3D, with their recipes Configuration the geyser's rhythm, the fall back, the dials; the /geyser command; the builders' tools

Skypiea sits above the overworld's deep oceans and nowhere else: its islands and its sea of clouds only exist where the overworld below is deep ocean. The cloud sea is a sea you swim in and sail on, with a swell; boats float on it. It is translucent: you see the fish under you. A fishing rod works in it, and an empty bucket takes a block of it away (the Sea Cloud Bucket).

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• Worldgen mods: Skypiea reads the overworld's own biomes to find the deep oceans (minecraft:is_deep_ocean) and changes nothing in the overworld beyond the geyser. Checked with Terralith and with TerraBlender + Biomes O' Plenty: geysers and islands appear as usual.
  • Fishing mods: a fishing rod works in the cloud sea, and what is caught is left to the game's own table or to any mod that listens to the fishing event. The cloud sea is still not water: it does not weaken a Devil Fruit user.
  • Biome tags, for other mods and datapacks: inosky:is_skypiea, inosky:is_cloud_sea, inosky:is_angel_island, inosky:is_upper_yard.
  • Valkyrien Skies 2 (optional, 2.4.11 or later): a ship sailed into an erupting Knock-Up Stream rises to Skypiea with its crew, lands on open cloud sea and floats on it. A ship that falls out of Skypiea goes back to the overworld with its crew. Anybody seated at the helm arrives standing on the deck. Sky Island never requires Valkyrien Skies.

docs.title: Angel Islands
docs.text: Two islands in three are Angel Islands: low islands made of island cloud from top to bottom, a few trees rooted in the cloud. Their shore is a cliff down to a flat shelf at the level of the cloud sea — Angel Beach.

docs.title: Skypiean villages
docs.text:
Every Angel Island has a village of houses in cloud brick, cut cloud and shell tiles, with streets edged in oak, lamp posts and a square. The larger islands have larger villages, with:

  • an inn, amber-roofed, with a bar, tables and rooms upstairs;
  • a dial shop, coral-roofed, its shells on show along the counter;
  • a bandstand;
  • kitchen gardens on cloud farmland;
  • a cloud fountain;
  • in one village in three, a climate terrace where Haredas teaches the Art of Weather.

docs.title: The houses
docs.text:
Five shapes: the family house under its gable, a two-storey house with a balcony, the fisherman's house with its catch drying under a long roof, a round house under a dome, and a house with a gallery. Each house draws its own colours: a roof of turquoise, coral, amber or lilac shell tiles, shutters and a door painted to match, and its own walls.

They are furnished: a table and chairs, a kitchen whose chimney smokes, beds, shelves, carpets, flowers at the windows.

docs.title: The Skypieans
docs.text:
The villagers are sky people of this mod: eight people, men and women, young and old, with small wings at the shoulders and their hair grown into antennae. The dial merchant is one of them, in a blue apron behind his counter; he sells the base mod's dials. The White Berets protect them.

Villages generated before 0.3.0 keep the base mod's Skypieans and their old houses.

docs.title: Cloud farmland
docs.text: A hoe tills island cloud into cloud farmland, and crops grow in it exactly as in farmland: water nearby keeps it moist — or sea cloud, which a Sea Cloud Bucket carries to your field — and trampled or left bare it turns back into island cloud.

docs.title: The village blocks
docs.text: Every block the villages are built from can be crafted: cloud brick, cut cloud, cloud pillars and walls, shell tiles in four colours, painted shutters and doors, awning cloth, cloud glass, conch lanterns and Vearth urns. Their recipes are on the Blocks page.

docs.title: The White Berets
docs.text:
Skypiea's police. Every village has their post — a small tower of white stone with battlements, a cell and a bell — with a rare chest of seized goods, and the White Beret Guards (the recruits) and a White Beret Captain who keep order in the village. Under the same uniform there are eight faces: skin, hair, eyes, a moustache, a beard or a scar. They are calibrated against the base mod's own NPCs — the captain is the stronger, with Busoshoku Haki.

The White Beret Captain

A White Beret Guard

docs.title: Angel Beach
docs.text:
The flat shore at the foot of an Angel Island's cliffs.

  • Dials wash up on the beach over time, a few at a time, and are picked up like any item. How often, and how many a stretch of beach holds, is in the configuration.
  • A seafront, once per village island, facing the island's geyser: the dial workshop under its lilac awning, a promenade along the shore, a pier, deck chairs, and sometimes a castle of cloud. Behind the workshop's counter stands the Waver Dealer, who sells the waver.
  • White Beret lookouts along the shore wherever it has room, never within 64 blocks of the seafront or of another lookout, each with its guard.
  • Sky Lobsters walk the beach (see Wildlife).

docs.title: Heaven's Gate
docs.text: The way into Skypiea, on every village island: the gate, its tunnel through the bank of cloud, and a causeway from the tunnel to the promenade. The geyser sets you down right in front of it.

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text:
Sky Island adds the clouds Skypiea is made of, the blocks its villages are built from — shell tiles, shutters, doors and awnings in four colours — and a few more: the weather cloud, the milky cloud of the roads, gilded stone bricks. Every village block can be crafted, so a Skypiean house can be built anywhere.

Turn a block round (drag), zoom (scroll or pinch), and pick another with the buttons:

docs.title: The clouds
docs.text: Block What it is How to get it Island Cloud The cloud you walk on: the ground of the Angel Islands and the surface of the cloud sea. Soft, quick to break, with the sound of wool. Dig it in Skypiea. Sea Cloud The body of the cloud sea. You do not stand on it: you swim in it, and falling into it does no harm. It is not water, so it does not weaken a Devil Fruit user. Take it with an empty bucket. Broken by hand, it drops nothing. Cloud Farmland Island cloud tilled with a hoe. Crops grow in it exactly as in farmland: water nearby keeps it moist, and trampled or left bare it turns back into island cloud. Use a hoe on island cloud. Broken, it gives island cloud back.

docs.title: The Sea Cloud Bucket
docs.text: An empty bucket used on a block of sea cloud takes it, as it takes powder snow; the Sea Cloud Bucket lays it back where you use it. One block a bucket: the cloud sea does not flow, so a bucket never makes a spring. A dispenser does both too. Sea cloud waters cloud farmland, so this is how the sea comes to a field.

docs.title: The village blocks
docs.text:
Everything starts from Island Cloud. A stonecutter makes each block one for one; the crafting grid makes several at a time.

Block What it is Crafting grid Stonecutter Cloud Brick The village walls: packed cloud sawn into bricks, harder than island cloud. 4 Island Cloud in a square → 4 Island Cloud Cut Cloud The smooth panel: lintels, frames, plinths and paving. 4 Cloud Brick in a square → 4 Island Cloud or Cloud Brick Cut Cloud Slab The half block of cut cloud. 3 Cut Cloud in a row → 6 Cut Cloud Cloud Pillar The column: it can stand or lie along any axis, like a log. 2 Cut Cloud, one on the other → 2 Cut Cloud Cloud Pillar Wall The slender column: a wall that joins its neighbours and stacks into a thin post. 6 Cloud Pillar, in two rows of three → 6 Cloud Pillar Shell Tile The roofs: scales of shell, the hardest block of the village. 8 Cut Cloud around 1 Cyan Dye → 8 — Shell Tile Stairs The slope of the roofs. 6 Shell Tile in a staircase → 4 Shell Tile Cloud Glass The windows: milky and barely see-through, but daylight passes. Smelt Island Cloud in a furnace — Awning Cloth The striped cloth over the market stalls: a slab, laid on posts. No creature spawns on it. Red Wool, White Wool, Red Wool in a row → 6 — Conch Lantern The village light. It stands on a block or hangs under one, and gives a little less light than a lantern (12 instead of 15). 8 Cut Cloud around 1 Torch → 1 — Vearth Urn A pot of Vearth, the earth Skypieans treasure: a decoration set by the doors. 3 Brick (the item) in a V, 1 Dirt between the top two → 1 —

docs.title: The other colours
docs.text:
A roof is turquoise, coral, amber or lilac, and the shutters, the door and the awning are painted to match. The turquoise shell tile and the red awning are the two above.

Block What it is Crafting grid Stonecutter Coral Shell Tile The roofs' other colours. 8 Cut Cloud around 1 Red Dye → 8 — Coral Shell Tile Stairs Its slope. 6 Coral Shell Tile in a staircase → 4 Coral Shell Tile Amber Shell Tile The roofs' other colours. 8 Cut Cloud around 1 Yellow Dye → 8 — Amber Shell Tile Stairs Its slope. 6 Amber Shell Tile in a staircase → 4 Amber Shell Tile Lilac Shell Tile The roofs' other colours. 8 Cut Cloud around 1 Purple Dye → 8 — Lilac Shell Tile Stairs Its slope. 6 Lilac Shell Tile in a staircase → 4 Lilac Shell Tile Turquoise Awning Cloth The awning, striped in another colour. Cyan Wool, White Wool, Cyan Wool in a row → 6 — Amber Awning Cloth The awning, striped in another colour. Yellow Wool, White Wool, Yellow Wool in a row → 6 — Lilac Awning Cloth The awning, striped in another colour. Purple Wool, White Wool, Purple Wool in a row → 6 —

Shutters and doors, in the four paints. They are wooden to the game: a hand opens them, and so do the villagers.

Shutter Door Recipe Turquoise Shutter Turquoise Door any wooden trapdoor, or any wooden door, with 1 Cyan Dye Coral Shutter Coral Door any wooden trapdoor, or any wooden door, with 1 Red Dye Amber Shutter Amber Door any wooden trapdoor, or any wooden door, with 1 Yellow Dye Lilac Shutter Lilac Door any wooden trapdoor, or any wooden door, with 1 Purple Dye

docs.title: More blocks
docs.text:
Block What it is How to get it Weather Cloud A cloud with a weather of its own: it drizzles, snows or blows a breeze. Click it with a snowball, a feather or a bucket of water to change its weather. Seen all over Weatheria. 2 Cut Cloud and a Water Bucket → 2 Milky Cloud The deck of the Milky Roads: creamy white, and it glows a little. Dig it on a road, with a shovel. Milky Curb The roads' edges: milky cloud a shade darker, ribbed. Dig it on a road. Gilded Stone Bricks Stone bricks inlaid with gold leaf: the walls of Shandora. 4 Stone Bricks around 1 Gold Nugget → 4

A recipe viewer (JEI or EMI) shows the same recipes in game.

The Knock-Up Core

The base of a Knock-Up Stream holds one more block, the Knock-Up Core: invisible, unbreakable, and never an item. It is the geyser's machinery, placed by the world itself. Server builders have a geyser they can place, the Knock-Up Stream block: see Configuration.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Every Sky Island release for Minecraft 1.20.1, newest first, as published on CurseForge.

docs.title: 0.3.0 (beta)
docs.text:
Released 2026-10-02 · Download

The biggest update so far. Weatheria, the weather scientists' floating island, with Haredas at home and weather for sale. Sky people of our own: Skypieans, White Berets and Shandias with their own faces and wings, and Shandias armed with bows, pistols, rifles and shields. The waver and the Milky Roads to travel between islands. A cloud sea you can see into, with fish in it. Three predators in the Upper Yards. Villages rebuilt, house by house. And Skypiea generates two to three times faster.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 4.0.0 or newer (was 2.6.1). Client and server.

⚠️ Still a beta: worlds are generated from this version's rules. Chunks already explored keep what they have. Everything new that belongs to the land (Weatheria, the Milky Roads, the new houses, the solid island feet) appears only in places you have not been to yet.

New: Weatheria
  • A floating island of four cloud tiers on a great glass bubble, green on top. Rare: about one for ten islands. It hangs over land as well as over the sea, and no geyser leads to it: fly there.
  • The scientists' town: Haredas's tower at the summit, pinwheel windmills, houses, the observatory's glass sphere, the Weather Ball garden and the balloon terminal, joined by white stairs with glass railings.
  • Paths and scenery: white promenades, lamp posts and benches facing the view, trimmed trees and cloud trees, flower beds, a snowy corner with its snowman, a sunny corner of sunflowers, a weather station.
  • Its people: old scientists in wizard robes and pointed hats, twelve looks. They keep to their homes and flee when struck.
  • Haredas, the master of the Art of Weather, as the anime shows him: blue robe, great white beard, floppy hat, small wings pointing down. He still teaches the Art of Weather, on Weatheria and on the climate terrace of the villages that have one (one village in three now).
  • Weather for sale: the Weather Vendor at the balloon terminal sells the weather of the Blue Sea below - clear sky (1,000,000 extol, 15 min), rain (1,500,000, 10 min) or a thunderstorm (3,000,000, 5 min). One sale a day at each booth.
  • Weather Cloud, a new block: it drizzles, snows or blows a breeze. Two cut clouds and a bucket of water make two; click one with a snowball, a feather or a bucket of water to change its weather.
  • Cloud foxes and sheep live on the island. Its chests hold a Devil Fruit box now and then.
New: sky people of our own
  • Wings of our own: small round-feathered wings for the Skypieans, long swept-back ones for the Shandias. They fold at rest, open when walking and beat in the air. The Shandias no longer wear the Skypieans' antennae.
  • Skypiean villagers: eight people, men and women, young and old, with their hair grown into antennae. The dial merchant is one of them, behind his counter - and still sells the base mod's dials.
  • White Berets: eight faces under the same uniform, for guards and captains alike.
New: armed Shandias
  • A warrior now carries one of six weapons: spear, bow, twin pistols, rifle, shield and spear, or bazooka. Each fights its own way: archers and gunmen keep their distance, the rifleman aims before he fires (you see his line of sight), the shield-bearer guards his front, walks ahead of the others and can send projectiles back.
  • Shandia Bow and Shandia Shield: two new items, usable by players.
  • The Shandia spear has a 3D model in hand, for players and warriors, and a redrawn icon.
  • Shandias never hit each other with their arrows and bullets.
New: the waver and the Milky Roads
  • The waver, Skypiea's cloud-sea scooter: one rider, standing at the handlebars. Faster than a boat (about 13 blocks a second against 8), it glides on cloud as on the sea and climbs one-block steps.
    • Craft it with an iron ingot, planks and a Breath Dial, or buy it from the Waver Dealer at the seafront's dial workshop.
  • Milky Roads: every island is now linked to its nearest neighbour by a road of milky cloud, five blocks wide. It follows the sea where there is one and bridges the void where there is none, then climbs onto the island.
New: life in the cloud sea
  • The cloud sea is translucent: you can see what swims in it.
  • Sky Fish in shoals, leaping out of the sea; the rare Balloon Sky Fish, floating with its back out; the Giant Sky Fish, whose fan cuts the surface; the Sky Lobster on the Angel Beaches. They drop fish.
  • A fishing rod works in the cloud sea: the bobber floats and fish bite.
  • Sea Cloud Bucket: an empty bucket takes a block of sea cloud, the full one lays it back, like powder snow. Sea cloud broken by hand no longer drops itself.
  • Sea cloud waters cloud farmland.
New: the predators of the Upper Yards
  • The Cloud Wolf: a wolf on two legs, in packs of two or three. It hunts players on sight, and a wolf that is struck calls its pack. It can be tamed with cooked meat (one try in three): it then follows you, fights for you and sits when told. Three coats. Weaker than a Shandia, but faster.
  • The Sky Shark: a shark that swims the air, in twos and threes. It goes for blood: a wounded player draws it from far away, and it will even turn on a wounded shark.
  • The Sky Lamprey: a giant that waits sunk in the ground, with only its ring of teeth showing. Come too close and it rises, bites and holds you in its mouth for three seconds. Strike it hard - you or a friend - and it lets go. Rare, alone, and as tough as a Shandia chief.
New: villages rebuilt
  • Five house shapes instead of three: the family house, a two-storey house with a balcony, the fisherman's house with its catch drying, a round house under a dome, a house with a gallery. Each draws its roof colour - turquoise, coral, amber or lilac - with shutters and a door painted to match, and its own walls.
  • Houses are furnished: table and chairs, a kitchen with a smoking chimney, beds, shelves, carpets, flowers at the windows.
  • The trades have their colours: an amber inn with a bar and rooms upstairs, a coral dial shop, a White Berets' post like a small white tower, a lilac dial workshop on the seafront.
  • Streets show: an oak border along the paving and lamp posts. Windows look like windows: cloud glass is redrawn with a wooden frame.
  • New blocks, all craftable: Coral, Amber and Lilac Shell Tiles and stairs; painted Shutters and Doors in four colours; Turquoise, Amber and Lilac Awning Cloth; Gilded Stone Bricks.
  • Seafront buildings now stand on their own stretch of beach instead of in the sea.
For server builders
  • Knock-Up Stream block (creative only): placed anywhere, it erupts with the geysers and sends whoever stands on it to Skypiea, at the same place.
  • An empty Skypiea: empty_skypiea = true in inosky-server.toml gives a Skypiea with no sea, no island and no geyser, to build your own. Set it before the world is first opened.
  • Public biome tags for other mods and datapacks: inosky:is_skypiea, is_cloud_sea, is_angel_island, is_upper_yard.
Changes
  • Skypiea generates two to three times faster. The land itself is unchanged.
  • Shandora gives about half the boxes it gave (4 a city instead of 8). The Golden Boxes are spared: more of the boxes you find are golden. This also reaches unopened chests in existing worlds.
  • Shandora's walls are inlaid with gilded stone bricks instead of blocks of gold. The crypt keeps its gold.
  • More lookouts and camps: an island gets a White Beret lookout wherever its shore has room, never beside another; an Upper Yard gets several Shandia camps wherever it has the clearings.
  • Compatibility checked: Terralith, and TerraBlender with Biomes O' Plenty - geysers and islands appear as usual.
Fixes
  • An island's foot is solid cloud: under the waterline an island was made of sea cloud, which you could sink into - and which looked like glass.
  • The Shandias' hidden village no longer sits partly on an island.
  • White Beret guards defend the villagers every time: a guard could ignore an attack that happened while he was stepping down a block.
  • Leaves no longer block the Giant Jack's ramp.
  • A piece of roof no longer floats in Shandora's great hall, and village counters and tables no longer hover over the floor.
  • Valkyrien Skies: a ship arriving by geyser is never set down across a Milky Road.

docs.title: 0.2.0 (beta)
docs.text:
Released 2026-09-26 · Download

Skypiea comes alive: its first animals. Giant South Birds that always face south, two birds you can tame, saddle and fly, the Cloud Fox and the huge Giant Dog as companions - the dog a mount too. And a round of fixes: every village island gets its Heaven's Gate, geysers keep their vent, and exploring Skypiea no longer floods the log.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.6.1 or newer (was 2.5.0). Client and server.

⚠️ Still a beta: worlds are generated from this version's rules. Chunks already explored keep what they have; islands you have not reached yet may get a Heaven's Gate they would not have had in 0.1.0 (see Fixes).

New: the birds of Skypiea
  • The giant South Bird (Upper Yards): the Jaya bird, grown huge on Skypiea and friendly. A living compass - once it stops, it turns to face south, beak and all.
  • The Sky Dot Bird (Pierre's kind) - pink and dotted, rare on the Angel Islands and in the Upper Yards - and the Three-Jo Bird (Fuza's kind) - a great lilac vulture, rarer still, in the Upper Yards only. Both are flying mounts:
    • tame them with seeds (like a parrot), then put a vanilla saddle on them;
    • only their owner rides and steers them;
    • fly like a horse that flies: the movement keys go the way you look, Jump climbs, Sneak descends, with neither they hover;
    • in the air, Sneak never drops you off - land first, then Sneak to get down;
    • fall out of Skypiea on one and you both go home, still in the saddle.
  • Their wings fold on the ground, beat fast when hovering or climbing, slow when cruising, and hold still in a dive; they bank into turns - with a rider too.
  • Drops: feathers and meat (cooked if they burned), more with Looting; a mount's saddle drops too.
New: companions
  • The Cloud Fox (Su's kind), on the Angel Islands: tame it with fish. It follows you, and lies down on the cloud when told to sit.
  • The Giant Dog (Holy's kind), very rare in the Upper Yards, huge: tame it with raw meat.
    • A guard, like a wolf: it goes for whatever strikes you and whatever you strike (never creepers, ghasts or your other animals), and catches up with you when it gets stuck in the trees.
    • A mount: saddle it and ride it like a horse - Jump leaps about three blocks. No fall damage under ten blocks.
    • 80 health, 8 attack damage.
  • Five coats each, the first the manga's own: fox cloud, sky, dawn, mint, dusk; dog cream, russet, silver, chocolate, charcoal.
Fixes
  • Geysers keep their vent: an amethyst geode next to a geyser could crush it. A geyser now repairs its crater by itself.
  • Heaven's Gate on every village island: about half of them had none. Where the gate needs the room, the beach's deck chairs, castle or workshop are left out.
  • You always arrive in front of the gate, never on its roof, even on a sloping coast.
  • Valkyrien Skies: a ship arriving by geyser no longer lands on Heaven's Gate; it looks further out for open cloud sea where the sea is shallow.
  • Exploring Skypiea is smoother: the game no longer fills its log with warnings each time new land appears, which slowed it down. The islands themselves are unchanged.
Known issues
  • Some Angel Islands have no White Beret lookout, or one oddly placed.
  • The Shandias' hidden village sometimes sits partly on an island instead of on the sea.
  • Some small Upper Yards have a single Shandia camp.
  • In a few worlds, leaves block the Giant Jack's ramp.

docs.title: 0.1.0 (beta)
docs.text:
Released 2026-09-24 · Download

The first release. A Forge addon for Mine Mine no Mi that adds Skypiea as a dedicated dimension, reached by riding a Knock-Up Stream up from the floor of the deep oceans: the cloud sea, the Angel Islands and their Skypiean villages, the beach, Heaven's Gate, and the Upper Yards with the Giant Jack, the ruins of Shandora and the Shandias.

Requires Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47+, Mine Mine no Mi 0.11.5 and AkumaLib 2.5.0 or newer. Client and server.

⚠️ The base mod's own sky islands no longer generate in the overworld: Skypiea replaces them. Structures already generated in an existing world stay where they are.

⚠️ A beta: worlds are generated from this version's rules. A later version may change where islands and structures stand in chunks not yet explored.

The way up: the Knock-Up Stream
  • A geyser on the floor of the deep oceans, one for each island above. Every ten minutes it rumbles for thirty seconds, then erupts for ninety (all configurable).
  • The column throws whatever is caught in it into the sky - players, mobs, dropped items, boats with their riders - and sends it on to Skypiea. An eruption always lasts long enough to carry somebody from the sea floor to the top.
  • You arrive on the ground or on the cloud sea, never inside a block: in front of Heaven's Gate on an island with a village.
  • /locate structure inosky:knock_up_stream finds one. /geyser tells where the nearest one is and when it erupts; /geyser now makes it erupt at once (operators).
The way down
  • Step off an island and sink through the cloud sea: below the bottom of Skypiea you come out high above the same place in the overworld, with slow falling. Boats come back too.
Skypiea
  • Islands only above the overworld's deep oceans; open cloud sea everywhere else above deep water, nothing above land.
  • The cloud sea: a sea of cloud you swim in, with a swell, bluish and animated so it is never mistaken for island cloud. Boats float and sail on it.
  • Its own sky, and no lava sea under it.
  • Island cloud, sea cloud and the Knock-Up Core are the dimension's own blocks; the Upper Yards are made of the overworld's earth and stone - the Vearth of the Blue Sea.
Angel Islands

Two islands in three: low islands of island cloud from top to bottom, a few trees rooted in the cloud. * Skypiean villages: houses of cloud brick, cut cloud and shell tiles, streets and a square, Skypiean civilians and traders (the base mod's own). Larger villages on the larger islands, with an inn, a bandstand, kitchen gardens and a cloud fountain. * Cloud farmland: a hoe tills island cloud, and crops grow in it exactly as in farmland. * The White Berets: their post in every village (with a rare chest of seized goods), recruits and a captain policing the village - calibrated against the base mod's NPCs. * The village blocks can be crafted: cloud brick, cut cloud, cloud pillars, shell tiles, awning cloth, cloud glass, conch lanterns, Vearth urns. * Angel Beach: the flat shore at the foot of the cliffs. Dials wash up on it over time. A seafront once per village island - the dial workshop, a promenade, a pier, deck chairs, sometimes a cloud castle - and one to three White Beret lookouts along the shore. * Heaven's Gate: the way into Skypiea on every village island - the gate, its tunnel, and a causeway to the promenade.

Upper Yards

One island in three, rarer and far larger: jungle plains around y 100, and massifs rising to about 215. * The Giant Jack (one Upper Yard in three): a beanstalk climbable to the top, a ramp up its whole height, and the Golden Bell at the summit with its chest - one or two boxes, a Golden Box in about two chests in five. * Shandora, the City of Gold (a little over half of the Upper Yards, sometimes beside a Giant Jack): its square, avenues and halls, the stepped temple and its altar, and the crypt under the Poneglyph - the treasure, one or two boxes a chest. Halls, altar and crypt all hold boxes now and then. * Small ruins of Shandora: one to three per Upper Yard in the jungle - an altar, a colonnade, a fallen house, a sacred well. * The Shandias: warriors and a chief guarding their land. They attack only looters - open their chests and they come for you. Their own weapons, the Shandia spear and the burn bazooka, and skills from dials (burn bazooka, impact, breath dash, sky step, the chief's reject). * Shandia war camps: two to four per Upper Yard, in clearings of the plains - four tipis round a fire, a totem, a weapon rack, a lookout. A chest in every tipi. * The hidden village: the Shandias' village in a pocket of cloud on the sea at the island's foot, opening on the sea - six tipis round a square, the statue of Kalgara, totems along the path, the chief by the fire.

Compatibility
  • Worldgen mods: Skypiea reads the overworld's own biomes to find the deep oceans (minecraft:is_deep_ocean) and changes nothing in the overworld beyond the geyser.
  • Valkyrien Skies 2 (optional, 2.4.11 or newer): a ship in an erupting Knock-Up Stream rises to Skypiea with its crew, lands on open cloud sea and floats on it; a ship that falls out of Skypiea goes back to the overworld with its crew. Sky Island never requires VS.
Configuration

<world>/serverconfig/inosky-server.toml: * geyser: cycle_ticks (12000), eruption_ticks (1800), charge_ticks (600); * return: return_y (-32), the height below which a body falls back to the overworld; * angel_beach: dial_chance (2000), dial_cap (2), how often dials wash up and how many a stretch of beach holds.

Known issues
  • An amethyst geode generated in a neighbouring chunk can crush a geyser's vent (#42).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Sky Island's settings are per world, in <world>/serverconfig/inosky-server.toml, created the first time the world is loaded with the mod. A save carries its own geyser rhythm.

Edit it with the world closed

Forge rewrites a world's server config when the world unloads: a change made while the game is running is lost. To see an eruption without waiting, use /geyser now instead.

docs.title: geyser
docs.text:
The Knock-Up Stream's rhythm. 20 ticks make a second.

Setting Default What it does cycle_ticks 12000 (10 minutes) Ticks between one eruption starting and the next. eruption_ticks 1800 (90 seconds) How long an eruption lasts. An eruption too short to carry somebody from the sea floor to the top is lengthened. charge_ticks 600 (30 seconds) The warning before an eruption: bubbles and rumbling.

docs.title: return
docs.text: Setting Default What it does return_y -32 Below this height in Skypiea, a body is given back to the overworld, above the same place. From -64 to 40.

docs.title: angel_beach
docs.text:
The dials the sea leaves on the shore of the Angel Islands.

Setting Default What it does dial_chance 2000 One random tick in this many, on a beach surface, lays a dial. 0 turns it off. dial_cap 2 The most dials a stretch of beach (8 blocks around) holds at once.

docs.title: The Knock-Up Stream block
docs.text: A geyser you place by hand: creative only (the Skypiea tab), no recipe, and it cannot be mined or blown up in survival. Placed on the sea floor or on dry land, it follows the geysers' rhythm, answers /geyser and /geyser now, and sends whatever stands in its column to Skypiea at its own X and Z. The arrival is yours to build there.

docs.title: builders
docs.text: Setting Default What it does empty_skypiea false true gives a Skypiea with nothing in it: no cloud sea, no island, no village, no animal, and no Knock-Up Stream in the overworld. The sky and the fall back to the overworld stay. Only chunks generated after the change follow it: set it before the world is first opened (in defaultconfigs/inosky-server.toml), or with the server stopped.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Permission What it does /geyser operator where the nearest geyser within 64 blocks is, what it is doing and when it erupts /geyser now operator makes that geyser erupt at once

docs.title: Getting around
docs.text: Skypiea's islands lie two to four thousand blocks apart, and most of the way between two of them is the void. Three ways to cross it: the waver on the sea, the Milky Roads on foot, and the flying mounts.

docs.title: The waver
docs.text:
Skypiea's cloud-sea scooter: a small wooden hull with a teal bow, a column with handlebars, and a Breath Dial for an engine.

  • One rider, standing at the handlebars. Mobs are never scooped up, as a boat does.
  • Faster than a boat: about 13 blocks a second, against 8 for a boat on the same sea.
  • It glides on cloud: on the islands' cloud skin and on the Milky Roads it slides as on the sea, and it climbs steps of one block.
  • A hard landing does not break it. Broken, it drops itself.

Getting one

Craft it an Iron Ingot over a Breath Dial between two Planks, over three Planks Buy it from the Waver Dealer, behind the counter of the seafront's dial workshop: 3 to 4 million extol. He also sells the base mod's dials.

The Breath Dial is the base mod's: it washes up on Angel Beach, and the dial merchants sell it.

docs.title: The Milky Roads
docs.text:
Every island is linked to its nearest neighbour by a road of milky cloud, five blocks wide, from centre to centre.

  • On the sea, the road rides the swell, flush with the surface.
  • Over the void, it is a bridge at the sea's level.
  • Reaching an island, it climbs onto it by a ramp.
  • It glows faintly at night.

A road stops short of what stands in its way — an island's cliffs, Heaven's Gate, a pier — and never crosses Weatheria. Roads appear in the parts of Skypiea explored with this version or later.

Milky Cloud and the Milky Curb along its edges are blocks: dig them with a shovel.

docs.title: The Knock-Up Stream
docs.text:
A Knock-Up Stream is a geyser on the floor of the deep ocean. There is one for every island in Skypiea, beside it below: a crater of dark prismarine and tuff round the Knock-Up Core.

/locate structure inosky:knock_up_stream

docs.title: An eruption
docs.text:
Phase Default What happens Quiet the rest of the cycle a bubble column marks the geyser Charge 30 seconds bubbles and rumbling: the warning Eruption 90 seconds the column rises to the sky

A cycle lasts ten minutes by default, and each geyser is offset in it by its own position: two geysers rarely erupt at the same moment. All three lengths are in the configuration.

The column lifts whatever is caught in it: players, mobs, dropped items, and boats with everyone aboard. At the top it sends them on to Skypiea. An eruption always lasts long enough to carry somebody from the sea floor to the top, whatever the configuration says.

docs.title: The arrival
docs.text: You come down on the ground or on the cloud sea, never inside a block. On an island with a village, the geyser sets you down in front of its Heaven's Gate; a boat arrives with its riders still in it.

docs.title: The way back
docs.text:
Step off an island and sink through the cloud sea. Below the bottom of Skypiea you come out high above the same place in the overworld, with slow falling long enough to land safely — over the sea, since Skypiea only lies above the deep oceans. Boats come back too.

The height of the fall back is return_y in the configuration.

docs.title: For operators
docs.text:
Command What it does /geyser where the nearest geyser within 64 blocks is, what it is doing and when it erupts /geyser now makes that geyser erupt at once

Server builders can also place a geyser of their own: the Knock-Up Stream block, on the Configuration page.

docs.title: Upper Yards
docs.text: One island in three is an Upper Yard: rarer and far larger than an Angel Island, made of the Blue Sea's earth — the Vearth the Skypieans revere. Jungle plains around y 100, and massifs of rock rising to about 215.

docs.title: The Giant Jack
docs.text: One Upper Yard in three has the Giant Jack: a beanstalk that towers over the island from its highest massif, climbable all the way up by a ramp around it. At the top hangs the Golden Bell, with a chest beneath it — one or two boxes, a Golden Box in about two chests in five.

docs.title: Shandora, the City of Gold
docs.text:
A little over half of the Upper Yards hold the ruins of Shandora, sometimes beside a Giant Jack (never within reach of its stalk): a square, avenues, halls, a broken tower, the stepped temple with its altar, and under the square the crypt beneath the Poneglyph.

Where What it may hold The halls gold, common dials, extols; a box in about one chest in seven The temple's altar gold, diamonds, emeralds, rare dials; a box in six chests in ten The crypt the treasure: gold, diamonds, netherite, very rare items, a heavy extol pouch — one box a chest, golden four times in ten

A whole city gives about four boxes, one of them golden. The walls are inlaid with gilded stone bricks; the gold itself is in the crypt.

Small ruins of Shandora lie in the jungle too, one to three per Upper Yard: a forgotten altar, a colonnade, a fallen house, a sacred well.

docs.title: The Shandias
docs.text:
The warriors of Shandora, and their chief, guarding their land. They attack only looters: leave their chests shut and they leave you alone.

A warrior (one of six looks)

The chief
  • Their skills, from dials: the burn bazooka, impact, a breath dash, a sky step, and the chief's reject.
  • Their arrows and bullets pass through other Shandias: they never hit their own.

A warrior carries one of six weapons; the chief keeps the bazooka.

Weapon How it fights Shandia spear (the commonest) hand to hand, with an impact dial Shandia bow keeps its distance (16 blocks); flame arrows, volleys Twin pistols keeps its distance (10 blocks), two bullets at a time; sidesteps Rifle from far away (24 blocks): aims for a second and a half — you see its line of sight — then fires a precise shot Shandia shield and spear guards its front and walks ahead of the others; bashes with the shield, and can send projectiles back Burn bazooka the burn bazooka's blast

The Shandia spear, the Shandia bow, the Shandia shield and the burn bazooka are items of this mod; a player can draw the bow and raise the shield. The spear has a 3D model in hand. Warriors never drop their weapons. - Few of them at a time: a chief and a warrior on Shandora's square, one in the temple, one in the tower.

docs.title: Shandia camps
docs.text:
War camps: two to four per Upper Yard wherever it has the clearings, in clearings of the plains, away from the city, the Giant Jack and the ruins. Four tipis round a fire, a totem, a weapon rack and a lookout, with two warriors.

The hidden village: the Shandias' own village, in a pocket of cloud on the sea at the island's foot, its only opening facing the sea. Six tipis round a square, the statue of Kalgara, totems along the path, and the chief by the fire.

There is a chest in every tipi: weapons, war dials, gold and emeralds, an extol pouch, food and arrows — and now and then a Wooden or an Iron Box.

docs.title: Predators
docs.text: The Upper Yards are hunting ground for three beasts: the Cloud Wolf, the Sky Shark and the Sky Lamprey. They are on the Wildlife page.

docs.title: Weatheria
docs.text:
The weather scientists' island. Unlike an Angel Island or an Upper Yard, it does not rise out of the cloud sea: it floats, a cake of four tiers of cloud, green on top, resting on a great glass bubble.

  • Rare: about one Weatheria for ten islands.
  • Over land as well as over the sea: it drifts where it likes, never above an island.
  • No Knock-Up Stream leads to it. Fly there on a Sky Dot Bird or a Three-Jo Bird; a Milky Road never crosses it.

docs.title: The scientists' town
docs.text:
Where What stands there The summit Haredas's tower: the control room with its instruments and a chest, his study upstairs The tiers pinwheel windmills, the scientists' houses, the observatory and its glass sphere, the Weather Ball garden The rim the balloon terminal, where the weather is sold

White stairs with glass railings and lantern posts join the tiers, two for each. White promenades run along every rim, with lamp posts and benches facing the view, and straight paths lead to every door.

Between the buildings: trimmed trees and cloud trees, blue and white flower beds, a snowy corner with its snowman under a snow cloud, a sunny corner of sunflowers, a weather station, and a line of Wind Knots near the tower. Cloud foxes and sheep live on the island.

Chests in the control room, the houses and the garden hold a Devil Fruit box now and then; the control room is the most generous.

docs.title: Its people
docs.text:
• Haredas, the master of the Art of Weather: a long blue robe, a great white beard, a tall hat whose tip flops over, and a Birkan's small wings pointing down. He teaches the base mod's Art of Weather, and keeps to his tower. He also lives on the climate terrace of one Skypiean village in three.
  • The scientists: old men in wizard robes and pointed hats, in twelve looks. Two in each house, one at the observatory and one in the garden. They never fight: they flee when struck, and keep to their homes.
  • The Weather Vendor, at the balloon terminal's booth.

docs.title: Weather for sale
docs.text:
Talk to the Weather Vendor to open his booth. He sells the weather of the Blue Sea below — the overworld, not Skypiea, where it never rains:

Weather Price Lasts Clear sky 1,000,000 extol 15 minutes Rain 1,500,000 extol 10 minutes Thunderstorm 3,000,000 extol 5 minutes

One sale a day at each booth: the screen shows how long the booth still rests.

docs.title: The weather cloud
docs.text:
A block of cloud with a weather of its own, seen all over Weatheria: a drizzle over the garden, snow over the snowy corner, a breeze out of every windmill.

  • Recipe: two Cut Cloud and a bucket of water give two weather clouds, drizzling.
  • Change its weather by hand: a snowball makes it snow, a feather makes it blow, a bucket of water brings the drizzle back. The snowball and the feather are used up; the bucket keeps its water.

docs.title: Wildlife
docs.text:
Skypiea's animals, after the manga: two birds you can ride, a living compass, two companions, the fish of the cloud sea, and the three predators of the Upper Yards. No vanilla monster spawns anywhere in Skypiea.

Animal Where Tamed with What it is South Bird Upper Yards, commonest — a living compass Sky Dot Bird Angel Islands and Upper Yards, rare seeds a light flying mount Three-Jo Bird Upper Yards only, rarer seeds a great flying mount Cloud Fox Angel Islands fish a companion Giant Dog Upper Yards only, very rare raw meat a guard and a mount

| Sky Fish, Balloon Sky Fish, Giant Sky Fish | the cloud sea | — | the fish of the sea | | Sky Lobster | Angel Beaches | — | a lobster on the beach | | Cloud Wolf | Upper Yards only | cooked meat | a predator, and a companion once tamed | | Sky Shark | Upper Yards only | — | a predator of the air | | Sky Lamprey | Upper Yards only, rare | — | a giant ambusher |

All of them have spawn eggs in the Skypiea creative tab.

docs.title: In 3D
docs.text: Drag to turn an animal round, scroll (or pinch) to zoom. The buttons under it show its coats, its saddle, and the birds on the ground.

docs.title: The South Bird
docs.text:
The bird of Jaya, grown huge on Skypiea (about two blocks tall), and friendly. It perches and takes to the air now and then. A living compass: whenever it stops, it swings round to face south, beak and all — a way to find your bearings on a sea of clouds.

The South Bird

docs.title: The flying mounts
docs.text:
The Sky Dot Bird (Pierre's kind) is pink and dotted, quick and a strong climber. The Three-Jo Bird (Fuza's kind) is a great lilac vulture with a salmon ruff: bigger and tougher, slower to climb.

The Sky Dot Bird

The Three-Jo Bird Sky Dot Bird Three-Jo Bird Health 30 50 Taming one seed in 5 one seed in 10 Wingspan about 4.5 blocks about 6.5 blocks
  1. Tame it with seeds (wheat, melon, pumpkin, beetroot or torchflower), like a parrot. Seeds also heal a tamed one.
  2. Saddle it: use a vanilla saddle on it. Without a saddle, a click makes it sit or stand.
  3. Ride it: use it with an empty hand. Only its owner can ride and steer it.

Sky Dot Bird, with a saddle

Three-Jo Bird, with a saddle

Flying it — a horse that flies:

Key In the air Movement keys fly the way you look Jump climb Sneak descend neither hover where you are

Getting off

In the air, Sneak descends and never drops you off. Land, then Sneak to get down. Holding Sneak all the way to the ground gets you off as soon as it touches down.

Below the cloud sea, the bird and its rider fall back to the overworld together, the rider still in the saddle. A mount takes no fall damage.

docs.title: The Cloud Fox
docs.text:
Su's kind: a small white fox with a long muzzle, on the Angel Islands. Tame it with fish (raw cod or salmon); it follows you, and lies down on the cloud when you click it. It never fights. 12 health.

The Cloud Fox

docs.title: The Giant Dog
docs.text:
Holy's kind: a huge dog — over three blocks tall — very rare in the Upper Yards. Tame it with raw meat (beef, pork or mutton).

The Giant Dog

With a saddle
  • A guard, like a wolf: it goes for whatever strikes you and whatever you strike — never creepers, ghasts or your other animals. It catches up with you by leaping to your side when it gets stuck in the trees.
  • A mount: put a vanilla saddle on it and ride it like a horse. The movement keys go the way you look; Jump leaps about three blocks. Ridden, it bites nothing of its own accord. Sneak + click still makes it sit or stand.
  • Tough: 80 health, 8 attack damage, hard to knock back, and no fall damage under ten blocks (half beyond).

docs.title: Coats
docs.text:
The fox and the dog are born in one of five coats and keep it for life; the first is the manga's own.

Coats Cloud Fox cloud (Su), sky, dawn, mint, dusk Giant Dog cream (Holy), russet, silver, chocolate, charcoal

docs.title: The cloud sea
docs.text:
The sea is translucent: its fish are seen from above, swimming close under the surface.

Creature Where How it shows itself Drops Sky Fish the cloud sea, in shoals of two to four leaps out of the sea a cod Balloon Sky Fish the cloud sea, rare floats with its back out of the sea a pufferfish Giant Sky Fish the cloud sea, far apart its fan cuts the surface, and it breaches now and then four to six cod Sky Lobster the Angel Beaches walks the beach a salmon

The Sky Fish

The Balloon Sky Fish

The Sky Lobster

None of them fights. They are not vanilla fish: the cloud sea is not water, and a vanilla fish would suffocate in it.

Fishing: a fishing rod works in the cloud sea — the bobber floats and fish bite. What you catch is the game's own fishing loot, unless another mod changes it.

docs.title: The predators of the Upper Yards
docs.text:
Three beasts hunt in the Upper Yards, and nowhere else. They are there with the land, like the birds, and attack nobody in Peaceful.

Predator How many Health Attack What it does Cloud Wolf packs of two or three 30 4 hunts on sight; can be tamed Sky Shark twos and threes, rarer 24 5 swims the air; goes for the wounded Sky Lamprey alone, rare 120 8 lies in wait, bites and holds

docs.title: The Cloud Wolf
docs.text:
A wolf that walks on two legs: lilac grey with a great white ruff and tail, narrow yellow eyes. Three coats: lilac (the manga's), storm and snow.

lilac

storm

snow
  • It hunts. A wild wolf goes for any player it sees, and a wolf that is struck calls its pack.
  • It can be tamed with cooked meat (beef, pork, mutton, chicken or rabbit): one try in three. A tamed wolf follows its owner, fights for them, sits when told, and no longer hunts players.
  • Weaker than a Shandia, but faster: one is a nuisance, three are a fight. 2 armor.
  • Drops: leather (none to two) and meat (one or two).

docs.title: The Sky Shark
docs.text:
A shark that swims the air a few blocks over the ground: long and thin, navy blue with pale tiger stripes.

The Sky Shark
  • It goes for blood. A player it sees within 12 blocks is prey; a wounded one — three quarters of their health or less — draws it from 32 blocks, and it leaves a whole prey for a bleeding one.
  • A wounded Sky Shark is prey to the others too.
  • Drops: one or two cod.

docs.title: The Sky Lamprey
docs.text:
A giant: a pale tube as thick as a tree, four and a half blocks tall, with a round maroon mouth ringed with teeth.

Risen

Striking
  • It lies in wait, sunk in the ground: only the ring of its teeth shows. It rises when a player comes within 7 blocks, and sinks back after ten seconds alone.
  • It bites and holds. Within 4.5 blocks of its foot it bites, lifts its prey off the ground in its mouth and holds it for three seconds, biting twice more. The prey cannot climb out.
  • A blow frees the prey: a hit of 4 damage or more on the lamprey — from the prey or from a friend — makes it let go at once. After a hold it rests five seconds.
  • It never moves from its spot and cannot be pushed. 4 armor: as tough as a Shandia chief.
  • Drops: three to five salmon.

docs.title: Drops
docs.text: The birds drop feathers and meat (cooked if they burned), more with Looting: one to three feathers and one or two pieces of meat from the South Bird and the Sky Dot Bird, two to five and two or three from the Three-Jo Bird. A saddled mount drops its saddle.
